docs.text: Silverlight360 documentation ¶ Silverlight360 builds C# and XAML Silverlight apps for the Xbox 360 Silverlight platform, the one Netflix, YouTube and the other Xbox 360 apps used. The output is a package with a default.xex you can run in the xenia-edge emulator. The code, samples and tools are at github.com/Digiex/Silverlight360 . Guides: Getting started Install the tools, make a runtime profile, build and run a sample. Projects and Visual Studio The project file, references, build properties, packaging, IntelliSense. App model Startup, XboxApplicationFrame , pages and navigation, back and exit, the TV screen. Input and focus Controller events, focus, moving focus with the D-pad, the Legend, media remotes. Xbox controls Pivot, Rune, Legend, MediaTransport, ContinuousList, transitions, speech. Networking WebClient and HttpWebRequest , cross-domain policy, what needs Xbox LIVE. Storage Saving settings in a storage container, the cache drive. Media MediaElement , MediaTransport , Smooth Streaming, DRM. Gamer services Signed-in gamers, the Guide, presence, threading. Native code Calling the kernel and XAM with DllImport . Testing in xenia Running an app with scripted controller input and screenshots. Status under xenia What works in the emulator today and what doesn't. Reference: API reference : the Xbox libraries and the Xbox additions to Silverlight, one page per namespace. The same text appears in Visual Studio's IntelliSense. Samples : what each sample shows and how it was tested. Runtime inventory : the platform versions found in the shipped apps. Everything here comes from running apps in the xenia-edge emulator and from reading the platform's own assemblies. Of the samples, only PageNavigation has been run on a console so far.

docs.text: App model ¶ Startup ¶ XamlHost ( default.xex ) starts the CLR, reads AppManifest.xaml , loads the entry assembly and creates the Application class named there. As in any Silverlight app, Startup sets RootVisual : private void Application_Startup(object sender, StartupEventArgs e) { RootVisual = new MainPage(); } The screen is 1280x720. Design pages at that size and keep important content inside the title-safe area, the inner 90% (64 pixels from the left and right, 36 from the top and bottom), because TVs crop the edges. XboxApplicationFrame ¶ Apps with more than one page use XboxApplicationFrame ( Microsoft.Xbox.Controls ) as the root. It's a navigation Frame that also: Starts GamerServices : it calls GamerServicesDispatcher.Initialize , then pumps GamerServicesDispatcher.Update and FrameworkDispatcher.Update every frame. Signed-in gamer information, the Guide, storage containers and MediaTransport 's screen-saver control depend on that. Initializes the UI sounds. Plays the page transitions set with TransitionService . Hosts the one VuiBar used for speech, in its template. private void Application_Startup(object sender, StartupEventArgs e) { var frame = new XboxApplicationFrame(); frame.Source = new Uri("/Pages/HomePage.xaml", UriKind.Relative); RootVisual = frame; } Without the frame, an app that uses gamer services or storage has to start GamerServices itself. The PlatformCalls sample does: if (!GamerServicesDispatcher.IsInitialized) { GamerServicesDispatcher.Initialize(null); } CompositionTarget.Rendering += delegate { FrameworkDispatcher.Update(); GamerServicesDispatcher.Update(); }; Pages and navigation ¶ Pages are XboxApplicationPage XAML files (a Page with Xbox transitions): <xbox:XboxApplicationPage x:Class="MyApp.Pages.HomePage" xmlns="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml/presentation" xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml" xmlns:xbox="clr-namespace:Microsoft.Xbox.Controls;assembly=Microsoft.Xbox"> ... </xbox:XboxApplicationPage> Navigate by URI. Parameters go on the query string and come back in NavigationContext.QueryString : NavigationService.Navigate(new Uri("/Pages/DetailPage.xaml?id=7", UriKind.Relative)); protected override void OnNavigatedTo(NavigationEventArgs e) { base.OnNavigatedTo(e); int id = int.Parse(NavigationContext.QueryString["id"]); Dispatcher.BeginInvoke(delegate { FirstButton.Focus(); }); } Every navigation creates a new page instance. Keep state that must survive in the App class or a static field, and focus something in OnNavigatedTo . Navigation is asynchronous. To go back several pages, call GoBack() again from the frame's Navigated event rather than in a loop, through Dispatcher.BeginInvoke so the back stack has settled. Detach the handlers when the walk ends, and also when a Navigating event comes with a NavigationMode other than Back . A handler left attached sends every later navigation back to the first page. On the console that happened a few pages deep. See App.GoHome in samples\ui\PageNavigation . Transitions ¶ XboxApplicationPage slides pages in and out ( ZIndexTransition ) by default. Elements marked with TransitionService.TransitionTarget="True" animate on their own, staggered by TransitionService.TransitionOrder , with each step 160 ms later: <TextBlock Text="Title" transitions:TransitionService.TransitionTarget="True" transitions:TransitionService.TransitionOrder="0" /> <Button Content="First" transitions:TransitionService.TransitionTarget="True" transitions:TransitionService.TransitionOrder="1" /> with xmlns:transitions="clr-namespace:Microsoft.Xbox.Transitions;assembly=Microsoft.Xbox" . Back and exit ¶ B is the back button by convention, and the app handles it. A frame-level handler sees B after the focused control has had its chance: frame.GamePadButtonDown += delegate(object s, GamePadButtonEventArgs args) { if (args.Button == GamePadButton.B && frame.CanGoBack) { frame.GoBack(); args.Handled = true; } }; Application.Current.Shutdown() , an Xbox addition, ends the app and returns to the dashboard. Shipped apps ask first (with Guide.BeginShowMessageBox ) when B is pressed on the first page. Unhandled exceptions ¶ An exception nobody catches reaches Application.UnhandledException . Unless the handler sets e.Handled = true , XamlHost quits to the dashboard. While developing, handle it and show the message on screen; the samples' App classes all do. Threading ¶ The UI thread runs the app. Network callbacks from WebClient arrive on the UI thread. Storage, cache container and gamer services callbacks ( Begin... / End... , ...Async completion events) arrive on other threads, so use Dispatcher.BeginInvoke before touching the UI (see Storage and Gamer services ).
docs.title: App model

docs.text: Xbox controls ¶ Microsoft.Xbox.dll has the controls the dashboard-style apps are built from. Use them with xmlns:xbox="clr-namespace:Microsoft.Xbox.Controls;assembly=Microsoft.Xbox" and a Microsoft.Xbox reference. The API reference documents every member; this page covers what you need to get them working. Their default styles come from the platform's theme. Some colors assume a light background (the Pivot headers are dark grey), so override templates where they don't fit. Pivot ¶ Sections side by side, one shown at a time, with the neighbours peeking in at the edges. The shoulder buttons switch sections. <xbox:Pivot x:Name="Sections"> <xbox:Pivot.HeaderTemplate> <DataTemplate> <TextBlock Text="{Binding}" FontSize="32" Foreground="#FFEBEBEB" /> </DataTemplate> </xbox:Pivot.HeaderTemplate> <xbox:PivotItem Header="browse"> <Grid>...buttons in rows and columns...</Grid> </xbox:PivotItem> <xbox:PivotItem Header="search">...</xbox:PivotItem> </xbox:Pivot> D-pad focus inside a section: each PivotItem moves it through the Grid it contains with the D-pad ( AutoGridNav , on by default). Give it a Grid with the controls in rows and columns. Focus when switching: focus the first control yourself in SelectionChanged . Lazy loading: LoadingPivotItem and UnloadingPivotItem are raised for items within two positions of the selection, so you can load section content on demand. Only one per page: a Pivot contains a SwipeViewer , and only one SwipeViewer can be active at a time. Don't put two Pivot s, or a Pivot and a ContinuousList , on one page. Samples: samples\ui\XboxControls , and samples\apps\CatalogBrowser , which builds its sections in code. Rune ¶ Text entry made for the TV: a strip of characters the user scrolls through with the D-pad and picks with A. X deletes and Y closes. It shows as a popup while IsOpen is true. <xbox:Rune x:Name="SearchRune" EmptyTextString="search for something" /> SearchRune.IsOpen = true; SearchRune.Focus(); SearchRune.TextChanged += delegate { Search(SearchRune.Text); }; A Rune also accepts text typed on a SmartGlass companion device. Under xenia the SmartGlass keyboard calls are missing, which only shows up in the log; typing with the controller works. Legend ¶ The A/B/X/Y hints at the bottom of the screen. See Input and focus . MediaTransport ¶ The Xbox video player's chrome: a transport bar, timeline, status and busy indicator, wired to a player. See Media . Set MediaAssetId before playback. Every command reports it, and commands throw InvalidOperationException without it. Needs GamerServices , for its screen-saver control; use it inside an XboxApplicationFrame . ContinuousList ¶ A horizontally paged list for long rows of items. It pages with the shoulder buttons, the D-pad, the remote's previous/next or a swipe, and raises ItemsInViewChanged . It contains a SwipeViewer , so the one-per-page rule applies. Transitions ¶ Page transitions and staggered element animations: see App model . Speech: VuiBar and VuiCommand ¶ Voice commands need a Kinect sensor, which xenia doesn't have, so none of this has been tested. From the code: XboxApplicationFrame 's template hosts the one VuiBar ; creating a second one throws. Build a VuiGrammar whose phrases' semantic values match each VuiCommand.SemanticValue , call LoadGrammar , add the commands, then StartRecognition . Grammars can't be loaded while recognition is running. Setting Localization.Culture unloads every grammar, the app's included; load them again afterwards. Kinect-only controls ¶ NuiTimeline scrubbing, SwipeViewer , DepthPIP and Rune gestures respond to the Kinect hand cursor. Without a sensor they still show, and the controller works with them.
docs.title: Xbox controls

docs.text: Gamer services ¶ Microsoft.Xbox.Services is the platform's build of XNA gamer services ( Microsoft.Xna.Framework.GamerServices ), with Xbox additions for Kinect versions of the system screens, social networks, presence and parental ratings. Starting it ¶ GamerServices has to be initialized, then pumped regularly. XboxApplicationFrame does both; without it, see App model . Sign-in changes, SignedIn and SignedOut , and Guide.IsVisible only update while it's pumped, and presence changes are only sent then. The signed-in gamer ¶ SignedInGamer gamer = Gamer.SignedInGamers.Count > 0 ? Gamer.SignedInGamers[0] : null; GamerText.Text = gamer != null ? "Signed in as " + gamer.Gamertag : "Not signed in"; samples\apps\CatalogBrowser shows the gamertag. Under xenia it's the emulator's profile name. System screens ¶ The XNA Guide methods, plus SignedInGamer.ShowFriends , ShowGamerCard , ShowComposeMessage , ShowParty and others, open the console's own screens. A few points: One at a time: only one system screen can be open; opening another throws GuideAlreadyVisibleException . Kinect versions: overloads that take a trackingId show the Kinect version of the screen for that tracked user. NuiGuide has the Kinect-required, controller-required and troubleshooting screens. Text limits: message boxes take 1 to 3 buttons, and titles, text and keyboard fields must be under 256 characters. Under xenia, most of these screens aren't implemented: the calls return without showing anything. Threading and async calls ¶ Completion callbacks of the Begin... / End... methods and of the ...Async events run on thread-pool threads, so use Dispatcher.BeginInvoke for UI. Many of the events are static and pass sender as null; use the userState argument to tell your requests apart. What needs Xbox LIVE ¶ Marketplace, purchase receipts, social network tokens and XAuth tokens need an Xbox LIVE sign-in, which isn't available, so they fail. Missing sign-in or privileges throws GamerPrivilegeException . PresenceModeString must be a mode defined in the title's LIVE configuration, or it throws ArgumentException . Parental controls ¶ ContentRating with CanAccess / CanAccessAsync , and SignedInGamer.GetRating , check content against the console's family settings.
docs.title: Gamer services

docs.text: Getting started ¶ What you need ¶ Windows with MSBuild 14 (Visual Studio 2015 or its Build Tools). Newer Visual Studio versions can open and build the projects too (see Projects and Visual Studio ). The Silverlight 3 tools and SDK , which provide the C# and XAML build tasks and the Silverlight 3 reference assemblies. Windows SDK 7.0A , which the Silverlight build tasks use. An extracted Xbox 360 Silverlight app . Every app ships its own copy of the platform, and the SDK builds against it. Plex has the newest platform of the shipped apps; the default profile uses Plex v0.0.0.7, a Games on Demand package ( tools\extract_god_packages.py extracts those). Python 3 for the test server and the extraction tools. xenia-edge with the Silverlight work to run the apps (see Status under xenia ). Optional, for IntelliSense text on the standard APIs: XNA Game Studio 4. Silverlight 3 is required anyway. 1. Make a runtime profile ¶ A runtime profile is the platform copied out of one app: the native host and runtime ( package\ ) and the framework assemblies to compile against ( reference\ ). Every build starts from it. .\tools\New-RuntimeProfile.ps1 -DonorApp '<extracted Plex v0.0.0.7>' -Output .\runtime\plex-2015 Use Plex v0.0.0.7, the base version Plex's last title update (v0.0.1.7) applies to. A package runs as the donor's title (Plex, 574407D1 ) at the donor's version. A console signed in to LIVE asks for an update when that version is older than the current one, and Plex's title update only applies to v0.0.0.7. Accept the update and the console installs Plex's title update, which then patches your package to v0.0.1.7 as it loads. The platform code is the same, and your app runs as before; xenia-edge does the same when that update is in its content folder. A profile made from the older v0.0.0.4 gets the update prompt but can't take the update. The script finishes by installing the IntelliSense files into reference\ ( tools\Install-ApiDocs.ps1 ; run it again after updating the SDK's docs). The profile holds Microsoft's and the donor app's binaries. It stays on your machine; runtime\ is ignored by git. 2. Build a sample ¶ .\tools\Build-XboxApp.ps1 -Project .\samples\ui\FocusNavigation\FocusNavigation.csproj The package lands in samples\ui\FocusNavigation\bin\Release\xbox\ . Its default.xex is the platform's host; your code is FocusNavigation.dll , plain IL next to it. 3. Run it ¶ xenia_edge.exe samples\ui\FocusNavigation\bin\Release\xbox\default.xex xenia_edge.exe is your xenia-edge build ( build\bin\Windows\Release in its folder). Use a controller, or xenia's keyboard input ( --hid=keyboard ): Shift+W/A/S/D is the D-pad, W/A/S/D the left stick, ; is A and ' is B (the last two depend on the keyboard layout). The samples that talk to a server need the test server running in another window: python samples\TestServer\server.py 4. Make your own app ¶ Copy a sample close to what you want; samples\ui\PageNavigation is a good start for a multi-page app. Then read Projects and Visual Studio and App model . Things that trip people up: Nothing has focus at startup. Controller input goes to the focused element, so focus something in Loaded or OnNavigatedTo . The D-pad doesn't move focus by itself outside a Pivot . Use the samples' DirectionalFocus helper or a PivotItem with a Grid (see Input and focus ). Unhandled exceptions quit the app. Set e.Handled = true in Application.UnhandledException while developing. Controls from Microsoft.Xbox need their assembly in the manifest. The SDK does this for every Xbox library you reference; don't mark those references Private=false . The title is the donor's. The package keeps the donor app's title ID and name, and with them its saved data.
docs.title: Getting started

docs.text: xenia_edge.exe samples\ui\FocusNavigation\bin\Release\xbox\default.xex xenia_edge.exe is your xenia-edge build ( build\bin\Windows\Release in its folder). Use a controller, or xenia's keyboard input ( --hid=keyboard ): Shift+W/A/S/D is the D-pad, W/A/S/D the left stick, ; is A and ' is B (the last two depend on the keyboard layout). The samples that talk to a server need the test server running in another window: python samples\TestServer\server.py
docs.title: 3. Run it

docs.text: Copy a sample close to what you want; samples\ui\PageNavigation is a good start for a multi-page app. Then read Projects and Visual Studio and App model . Things that trip people up: Nothing has focus at startup. Controller input goes to the focused element, so focus something in Loaded or OnNavigatedTo . The D-pad doesn't move focus by itself outside a Pivot . Use the samples' DirectionalFocus helper or a PivotItem with a Grid (see Input and focus ). Unhandled exceptions quit the app. Set e.Handled = true in Application.UnhandledException while developing. Controls from Microsoft.Xbox need their assembly in the manifest. The SDK does this for every Xbox library you reference; don't mark those references Private=false . The title is the donor's. The package keeps the donor app's title ID and name, and with them its saved data.
docs.title: 4. Make your own app

docs.text: Input and focus ¶ Controller events ¶ The Xbox runtime adds controller events to every UIElement ( System.Windows , namespace System.Windows.Input ): Event Arguments GamePadButtonDown , GamePadButtonUp GamePadButtonEventArgs.Button : A, B, X, Y, the D-pad directions, the shoulders, Start, Back, and the stick clicks. GamePadThumbStickMoved Side (left or right), XPosition and YPosition . Each runs from -1 to 1; Y is positive up. GamePadTriggerMoved Side , Position from 0 (released) to 1 (fully pulled). MediaCommand MediaCommandEventArgs.MediaCommand : play, pause, fast forward and the rest, from a media remote. They are routed events : raised on the element with focus, then bubbling up through its parents, like KeyDown . Set e.Handled = true to stop one. The guide button never reaches apps. GamePadButtonDown += delegate(object sender, GamePadButtonEventArgs e) { if (e.Button == GamePadButton.Y) { ShowDetails(); e.Handled = true; } }; GamePadButtonDownEvent and GamePadButtonUpEvent are also exposed as RoutedEvent s, for AddHandler(..., handledEventsToo: true) . The stick and trigger events aren't. samples\ui\GamepadInput shows every event live. Focus ¶ With nothing focused, no element gets controller input. A UserControl isn't focusable by default, so either set IsTabStop = true on it and call Focus() , or focus a control, in Loaded or OnNavigatedTo : Loaded += delegate { FirstTile.Focus(); }; After a navigation, focus from Dispatcher.BeginInvoke so the page is in the tree first. What the runtime does on its own ¶ A clicks the focused Button . Start and the remote's play/pause command do too, and the event is marked handled. Click arguments are an InputModalityRoutedEventArgs ; its InputModality says whether the click came from the controller, voice, a Kinect gesture, a remote, the keyboard or the mouse. The D-pad doesn't move focus between plain controls. In testing, pressing the D-pad over a Grid of Button s left focus where it was. PivotItem does move focus. With AutoGridNav (on by default), a PivotItem moves focus through the Grid it contains with the D-pad, and the Pivot changes items with the shoulder buttons. ContinuousList pages with the shoulder buttons and D-pad. See Xbox controls . Moving focus yourself ¶ For layouts outside a Pivot , the samples include samples\Common\DirectionalFocus.cs . Turn it on for a panel and the D-pad and left stick move focus to the nearest focusable control in that direction: <UserControl xmlns:sdk="clr-namespace:XboxSdk.Samples" ...> <Grid sdk:DirectionalFocus.IsEnabled="True"> ...buttons... </Grid> </UserControl> It considers every visible, enabled control with IsTabStop set among the panel's descendants. It picks the closest one in the pressed direction, preferring ones lined up with the current control. Disabled controls and IsTabStop="False" ones are skipped. Add the file to your project with <Compile Include="...\Common\DirectionalFocus.cs" /> . samples\ui\FocusNavigation shows it on a grid with a wide tile, a disabled one and one that isn't a tab stop. Showing focus ¶ TV users only know where they are from the focus visual, so make it obvious: a filled background, a frame, a slight zoom. Every sample's Button template has a FocusStates group with a green fill or frame in Focused . The Legend ¶ Legend ( Microsoft.Xbox.Controls ) shows what A, B, X and Y do. It reads attached properties from the focused element, or its nearest ancestor that has them: <Button Content="Watch list" xbox:Legend.AButtonText="open" xbox:Legend.XButtonText="clear list" /> ... <xbox:Legend HorizontalAlignment="Right" VerticalAlignment="Bottom" /> The attached properties can only be set on a Button , Pivot , ContinuousList , XboxApplicationFrame , Rune or NuiScrollViewer . Setting them on anything else throws. The Legend hides itself while the user is using Kinect gestures. Media remotes ¶ A media remote's buttons arrive as MediaCommand events on the focused element. MediaTransport handles them itself. For your own player, handle UIElement.MediaCommand and switch on e.MediaCommand . Kinect and speech ¶ Kinect gestures drive a hand cursor that arrives as mouse events: hovering a Button focuses it, and holding the hover clicks it. Speech commands ( VuiBar , VuiCommand , VuiGrammar ) need a Kinect sensor. Neither has been tested; xenia has no Kinect.

docs.text: Media ¶ Under xenia-edge, media plays once the console's codec modules are installed. Everything around the player works: MediaTransport , its transport bar and its commands. WMA plays as is: its decoder is built into the runtime. WMV , MP3 and MP4 need the console's extra AV codecs. The runtime gets their decoders from dash.ExtraAVCodecs.xex , a module of the console's system software that it loads through xam ( XamLoadExtraAVCodecs ). Without it, playback fails with MediaFailed "4001 An error has occured" right after Opening . Despite that code's name ( AG_E_NETWORK_ERROR ), the network isn't involved: the real error is C00DF804 for WMV (no video decoder) and 8007000E for MP3. Loading the module needs a xenia-edge build with the codec loader, pull request #329 , which isn't merged yet; with it, copy dash.ExtraAVCodecs.xex and dash.ExtraAVCodecs2.xex from your console's system files to xenia's system\ folder (next to content\ ). WMV (VC-1) and MP3 then play. MP4 (H.264/AAC) also needs the console's Optional Media Update, a content package (machine-wide content of type 2 for title FFFE07DF) that isn't part of the system update. Without it, the runtime shows the "media update required" screen when playback starts, and that can't complete without Xbox LIVE. Install it by copying the package file to xenia's content\0000000000000000\FFFE07DF\00000002\ . With both, MP4 plays, but the picture is wrong: green blocks over the right base colour, because xenia doesn't support a texture format ( k_32 ) the H.264 output uses. The first MP4 playback also waits for xenia to compile some very large shaders. To test without a server, put media files in samples\apps\MediaPlayer\Media and rebuild; the sample lists them as "(in the package)" and plays them from a URI relative to the XAP. The rest of this page is from the platform's code and the shipped apps. MediaElement ¶ The standard Silverlight MediaElement , playing WMV, WMA, MP4 (H.264/AAC) and MP3 over progressive download, plus Smooth Streaming through SmoothStreamingMediaElement . The Xbox version adds DRM and output-protection members (see the reference ). MediaTransport ¶ MediaTransport ( Microsoft.Xbox.Controls ) is the playback chrome every video app uses. It provides: the transport bar (play/pause, skip, rewind, fast forward, stop, info, display mode), the timeline, status text and busy indicator, controller and remote handling. Put the player inside it: <xbox:MediaTransport x:Name="Transport" Back="Transport_Back"> <MediaElement x:Name="Player" AutoPlay="True" /> </xbox:MediaTransport> protected override void OnNavigatedTo(NavigationEventArgs e) { base.OnNavigatedTo(e); Transport.MediaAssetId = "episode-42"; // required, see below Player.Source = new Uri(url, UriKind.Absolute); Dispatcher.BeginInvoke(delegate { Transport.Focus(); }); } private void Transport_Back(object sender, EventArgs e) { NavigationService.GoBack(); } What it handles itself: Controller: A, Start or the D-pad shows the transport bar. The triggers rewind and fast forward. The shoulder buttons skip between chapter markers. B hides whatever is showing and raises Back when nothing is left. Remote commands: they go through ExecuteMediaCommand . Fast forward and rewind: they're emulated. The player pauses and the timeline previews ahead, then seeks when you resume. Required: set MediaAssetId before any command. Each command is reported with it (for SmartGlass and usage statistics) and throws InvalidOperationException without it. Side effects while it's loaded: Media app status: it tells the console a video is playing, so the dashboard treats the app as a media app. SmartGlass: it reports position and state for companion devices on every command and state change. Screen saver: it suppresses the screen saver during playback. This needs GamerServices, so use it inside XboxApplicationFrame . samples\apps\MediaPlayer plays files from the test server's media folder. Smooth Streaming ¶ SmoothStreamingMediaElement ( Microsoft.Web.Media.SmoothStreaming ) plays adaptive streams: Source: set SmoothStreamingSource to a .../Manifest URL. Setting Source (progressive) throws NotSupportedException on Xbox. Set first: set SmoothStreamingPlaybackMode , SmoothStreamingCache , CookieContainer and LivePlaybackStartPosition before the source. Events: ManifestReady comes before MediaOpened . Restrict tracks with StreamInfo.RestrictTracks only in ManifestReady ; SelectTracks works at any time. Errors: after SmoothStreamingErrorOccurred the source is shut down; set it again to retry. Trick play: SetPlaybackRate only takes the values in SupportedPlaybackRates . Wrap it for MediaTransport with SmoothStreamingMediaElementAdapter . DRM ¶ PlayReady-protected content goes through LicenseAcquirer and MediaElement.LicenseAcquirer , as in Silverlight. VideoOutputConnector.EngageHdcpAsync and EngageCgmsaAsync turn on output protection before protected playback. None of this has been tested.
docs.title: Media

docs.text: Native code ¶ App code can call the console's kernel and system library directly with DllImport ; samples\NativeProbe does. Xbox modules export by ordinal only, so name the module and give the ordinal as #<decimal ordinal> , the way the platform's own assemblies import from agcore.dll and npctrl.dll : using System.Runtime.InteropServices; static class NativeMethods { // xam ordinal 0x282: DWORD XamGetSystemVersion() [DllImport("xam.xex", EntryPoint = "#642")] public static extern uint XamGetSystemVersion(); // xboxkrnl ordinal 0x84: VOID KeQuerySystemTime(PLARGE_INTEGER) [DllImport("xboxkrnl.exe", EntryPoint = "#132")] public static extern void KeQuerySystemTime(out long fileTime); } What the probe found under xenia-edge: No special permission needed: plain app code may call these, with no [SecurityCritical] or other attribute. Module names: xam.xex (or xam ) and xboxkrnl.exe both resolve. Data layout: the process is big-endian PowerPC, so integers, out / ref parameters and pointers are already in the layout the kernel expects. Pointers are 32-bit. A wrong entry point doesn't throw. A name instead of an ordinal, or a wrong ordinal, becomes a call through a null pointer, and XamlHost quits. Take ordinals from xenia's src/xenia/kernel/xam/xam_table.inc and src/xenia/kernel/xboxkrnl/xboxkrnl_table.inc . How the platform reaches native code ¶ The framework itself calls native code in these ways: agcore.dll by ordinal: System.Windows ' MS.Internal.XcpImports , for UI, media, DRM and downloads. npctrl.dll by ordinal: Microsoft.Xbox classes ( VuiManager , Kinect , Companion , MediaTransport , MediaCapabilities , DeviceDiscovery , ...) and System.Windows ' output protection. XamlHost extensions by name: DllImport("Net"|"STORAGE"|"AUDIO"|"MEDIA"|..., EntryPoint = "Name") . XamlHost registers a table of named functions per extension at startup. Gamer services go through one of them, Net!GamerServices_DispatchCommand_Entrypoint , which takes a command number. xadvertising.xex by ordinal: the advertising SDK. The CLR's internal calls into xcoreclr.dll . App code could call the XamlHost extensions the same way, but that hasn't been tried; their signatures have to be read from the decompiled Microsoft.Xbox.* assemblies.

docs.text: Networking ¶ WebClient and HttpWebRequest work as in Silverlight 3. The runtime sends the requests through the console's HTTP stack (XHttp); in xenia-edge that's the host's WinHTTP, so 127.0.0.1 is the PC running the emulator. var client = new WebClient(); client.DownloadStringCompleted += delegate(object sender, DownloadStringCompletedEventArgs e) { if (e.Error != null) { ShowError(e.Error); return; } Show(XDocument.Parse(e.Result)); }; client.DownloadStringAsync(new Uri("http://127.0.0.1:8360/api/catalog")); WebClient completion events arrive on the UI thread. samples\Common\ServerClient.cs wraps GET and POST. Cross-domain policy: as with any Silverlight app, a server on another host must allow access with /clientaccesspolicy.xml or /crossdomain.xml . The test server serves both. Data formats: the platform has no JSON serializer. Use XML with System.Xml.Linq , as the samples do, or ship a JSON library compiled for Silverlight 3. Images: BitmapImage takes a URI or a stream; WebClient.OpenReadAsync gets the bytes if you want to cache them (see PosterCache in samples\apps\CatalogBrowser ). Xbox additions to HttpWebRequest : IsAuthCall , LimitDownloadBufferSize and AllowLocalConnections are passed to the native stack. The last two can't be set once the request has been sent. Xbox LIVE and XAuth ¶ Requests to partner services were authenticated with XAuth tokens from Xbox LIVE ( Microsoft.Xbox.Security.XAuth : call XAuthService.Start , then use XAuthTokenRequest ; each request object can be used once). There's no Xbox LIVE to get tokens from, so anything behind XAuth fails. That includes sign-in for many of the shipped apps, Marketplace and social network tokens. Plain HTTP and HTTPS to your own servers work. The test server ¶ samples\TestServer\server.py serves what the samples need: Endpoint GET /api/hello , GET /api/time , POST /api/echo HelloXbox GET /api/catalog , GET /images/<id>.png CatalogBrowser: an XML catalog of made-up shows and generated posters GET /api/media , GET /media/<file> MediaPlayer: the files in samples\TestServer\media , with byte ranges It prints every request, so you can see what an app asks for.
docs.title: Networking

docs.text: Projects and Visual Studio ¶ The project file ¶ An app is a Silverlight 3 class library that imports the SDK's targets instead of Silverlight's: <Project ToolsVersion="4.0" DefaultTargets="Build" xmlns="http://schemas.microsoft.com/developer/msbuild/2003"> <PropertyGroup> <Configuration Condition=" '$(Configuration)' == '' ">Release</Configuration> <OutputType>Library</OutputType> <AssemblyName>MyApp</AssemblyName> <RootNamespace>MyApp</RootNamespace> <SilverlightAppEntry>MyApp.App</SilverlightAppEntry> <OutputPath>bin\$(Configuration)\</OutputPath> </PropertyGroup> <ItemGroup> <Reference Include="mscorlib" /> <Reference Include="System" /> <Reference Include="System.Core" /> <Reference Include="System.Windows" /> <Reference Include="System.Windows.Controls.Navigation" /> <!-- pages and Frame --> <Reference Include="Microsoft.Xbox" /> <!-- Xbox controls --> <Reference Include="Microsoft.Xbox.Core" /> <!-- XNA basics, PlayerIndex --> <Reference Include="Microsoft.Xbox.Services" /> <!-- gamer services --> <Reference Include="Microsoft.Xbox.Storage" /> <!-- storage and cache containers --> </ItemGroup> <ItemGroup> <ApplicationDefinition Include="App.xaml"><Generator>MSBuild:Compile</Generator></ApplicationDefinition> <Page Include="MainPage.xaml"><Generator>MSBuild:Compile</Generator></Page> <Compile Include="App.xaml.cs"><DependentUpon>App.xaml</DependentUpon></Compile> <Compile Include="MainPage.xaml.cs"><DependentUpon>MainPage.xaml</DependentUpon></Compile> </ItemGroup> <Import Project="path\to\Silverlight360\msbuild\XboxSilverlight.targets" /> </Project> References name assemblies only. The SDK resolves them from the runtime profile's reference folder, never from desktop Silverlight, so the Xbox additions ( UIElement.GamePadButtonDown , Application.Shutdown , ...) are there to compile against. Available assemblies: Assembly What's in it mscorlib , System , System.Core , System.Net , System.Xml The .NET base, with Xbox additions (see the reference). docs.text: Xbox 360 Silverlight runtime inventory ¶ Survey of the 79 Games on Demand packages extracted with tools\extract_god_packages.py . 68 of them are Silverlight apps (they ship agcore.dll ). The rest are native apps (Last.fm, ESPN, MLB.TV, Video Kinect and similar) that only use a few small XEX files. The raw data is in app-inventory.json and comes from tools\Get-AppInventory.ps1 . What every Silverlight app carries ¶ Each app ships the whole platform next to its own code: Piece Files Role XamlHost default.xex Native host the console launches. Reads AppManifest.xaml , loads the CLR and Silverlight, services Xbox calls (gamer services, storage, audio, media). CLR xcoreclr.dll The .NET runtime. Compiles IL itself when an assembly has no native image. Silverlight core agcore.dll , npctrl.dll , captions.dll Rendering, XAML, media, networking (through xam's XHttp). Framework mscorlib , System* , Microsoft.Xbox* , Microsoft.Web.Media.SmoothStreaming IL assemblies plus .ni.dll Xenon native images. Data fonts, SystemSounds , Config\machine.config , nuisp* speech databases, NuiIdentity.bin.be , Database.xmplr Platform resources. All framework assemblies report assembly version 2.0.5.0 and the deployment runtime is 3.0.40818.0 (Silverlight 3), so the real differences are in build dates and file versions. Runtime generations ¶ CLR build XamlHost SDK Apps Notes 2011-09-29 2.0.20951 Xbox LIVE Dailymotion Oldest. 2011-11-09 2.0.21076 35 apps incl. YouTube, Netflix, Hulu Plus, Disney XD Launch wave. Framework 3.7.60901 / 4.1.11119. 2012-03-08 2.0.21076 Fox, NOW TV, GameSpot TV, Sony Pictures 2012-05-09 2.0.21173 CNET, Blip, WSJ, Quickflix, Mustang Customizer, ... 2012-07-18 2.0.21173 - 2.0.21256 21 apps incl. Vimeo, GameTrailers, MTV, Plex Last CLR build (file version 4.0.338.9242). Every CLR build decompresses to the same 4.8 MB image; the 1.6 MB vs 4.8 MB file sizes only reflect XEX compression. None of them ship a separate xclrjit.dll , yet they run IL with no native image (see below). Newest and most complete: Plex (Dec 2013) ¶ Component Plex MTV (May 2013) GameTrailers / Vimeo (Nov 2012) YouTube (Nov 2011) XamlHost SDK 2.0.21256 2.0.21250 2.0.21250 2.0.21076 agcore / npctrl 2013-12-17 2013-05-30 2012-11-08 2011-11-19 CLR / mscorlib 4.0.338.9242 4.0.338.9242 4.0.338.9242 4.0.337.5446 System.Windows, System.Net 4.1.31216 4.1.30530 4.1.21107 3.7.60901 Microsoft.Xbox, .Core, .Services, .Storage 4.1.31216 4.1.30530 4.1.21107 3.7.60901 / 4.1.11119 Plex has the newest build of every platform component and all the commonly used framework assemblies, so the SDK's default runtime profile ( runtime\plex-2015 ) is made from it. Assemblies only a few apps carry: Assembly Where Notes Microsoft.Advertising 5.2 37 apps Ad SDK, needs xadvertising.xex . Microsoft.Xbox.Sample.* ~38 apps Microsoft's sample media app framework (UI, player, models). Microsoft.Xbox.Epg Revision3, WWE Program guide. Microsoft.Xbox.Extensions Netflix System.Xml.Serialization EPIX XBoxLiveLV YouTube LIVE sign-in helpers. These are app-level libraries, not part of the platform; a profile can carry them if an app needs one, but they aren't included by default. Native images are optional ¶ The Xbox CLR runs an assembly's IL when its .ni.dll is missing. YouTube with YouTubeXBoxApplication.ni.dll removed still runs its own startup code (the xbox_startup ping to youtube.com), and the SDK's sample app runs with no native image at all. Framework native images are kept because the platform ships them and they load faster.

docs.text: Samples ¶ Build any sample with tools\Build-XboxApp.ps1 -Project <csproj> and run its bin\Release\xbox\default.xex in xenia. Code shared by several samples is in samples\Common : ServerClient (HTTP), DirectionalFocus (D-pad focus movement) and DebugLog (debug output to xenia's log; see Testing ). UI samples ¶ Sample Shows Tested in xenia ui\GamepadInput Every controller event live: button down/up, both sticks, both triggers, how bubbling and Handled work, Application.Shutdown on Back+Start. Y, X, D-pad, RB, left stick and left trigger events shown live. ui\FocusNavigation Focus on a grid of tiles: a focused-state template, A clicking the focused Button , D-pad and stick movement with DirectionalFocus , disabled and non-tab-stop controls skipped, unused buttons bubbling to the page. D-pad and stick moved focus across the grid, including onto the wide tile; A clicked. ui\XboxControls Pivot sections switched with LB/RB and built-in grid navigation, a Rune for text entry, a Legend following the focused control. Focus moved by the PivotItem; RB switched sections; the Rune typed "bc"; the Legend changed with focus. ui\PageNavigation XboxApplicationFrame with XboxApplicationPage s, query-string parameters, staggered transitions, B for back, going back to the first page. Opened a page, went one deeper, B went back; four pages deep, "Back to the start" unwound to the home page and the home buttons still opened pages. Application samples ¶ Sample Shows Tested in xenia apps\CatalogBrowser A streaming-style catalog: an XML catalog from a server, a Pivot per category built in code, posters cached on the cache drive, a detail page, favourites saved in a storage container (Y toggles them), the signed-in gamertag, a Legend . Needs the test server. Catalog and posters loaded; gamertag shown; Y added a favourite and the detail page saw it; posters came from the cache drive on later loads; B went back; RB switched categories. apps\MediaPlayer A media list and a player page with MediaTransport around a MediaElement : MediaAssetId , focus, the Back event, stopping on leaving, state changes and failures logged with DebugLog . Lists files packaged in its Media folder (played from a URI relative to the XAP) and files from the test server's samples\TestServer\media . List, player page, transport bar and back work; WMA plays from the package and the server. With the codec loader and the console's codec module (see Media ), packaged WMV and MP3 play too; MP4 plays with a garbled picture. Earlier samples ¶ Sample Shows HelloXbox The smallest app: XAML, A on the controller, HTTP GET and POST to the test server, a DebugLog line at startup. NativeProbe DllImport into xam and the kernel by ordinal. PlatformCalls A storage container, the cache drive and MediaTransport commands, each reporting OK or the error. Written to test the xenia fixes for them. Screenshots ¶ All taken in xenia-edge. HelloXbox GamepadInput FocusNavigation XboxControls PageNavigation CatalogBrowser MediaPlayer , the list MediaPlayer , a WMV playing PlatformCalls

docs.text: Storage ¶ Two places to keep data, both from Microsoft.Xbox.Storage ( Microsoft.Xna.Framework.Storage ): Storage container Cache container Use for Settings, favourites, PINs, resume positions Downloaded images and responses Lives on The title's save area for the user The console's cache partition Survives Until the user deletes it Until the console clears the cache Encrypted Yes, per console No At a time Any number One per app The runtime host doesn't implement isolated storage (its isolated-storage callbacks return "not implemented"), so use these instead of IsolatedStorageFile . Both need GamerServices running; XboxApplicationFrame starts it (see App model ). Storage container ¶ var device = new StorageDevice(); device.BeginOpenContainer("My App", "MyApp", delegate(IAsyncResult ar) { // The callback runs on another thread. Deployment.Current.Dispatcher.BeginInvoke(delegate { using (StorageContainer container = device.EndOpenContainer(ar)) { using (Stream stream = container.CreateFile("settings.xml")) { settings.Save(stream); } } }); }, null); CreateFile and OpenFile return streams that encrypt and decrypt with a key bound to the console, so saved files can't be read on another console. FileExists , DeleteFile , GetFileNames and the directory methods work like System.IO . Open the container when you need it and dispose it afterwards. Favorites in samples\apps\CatalogBrowser wraps this pattern. Cache container ¶ CacheContainer.BeginOpenCacheContainer(delegate(IAsyncResult ar) { Deployment.Current.Dispatcher.BeginInvoke(delegate { cache = CacheContainer.EndOpenCacheContainer(ar); // keep it open }); }, null); One at a time: opening a second container while one is open throws InvalidOperationException . Open it once and keep it for the session, as PosterCache in samples\apps\CatalogBrowser does. It may disappear: the console can clear the cache partition at any time, so treat anything in it as re-downloadable. Cluster size: BeginOpenCacheContainer(format, bytesPerCluster, fileCacheSize, ...) sets the cluster size (4 KB to 64 KB, 4 KB by default). The drive is formatted when the size doesn't match. Unmounting: disposing the container unmounts the drive. Tested ¶ samples\PlatformCalls writes and reads back a file in each kind of container. samples\apps\CatalogBrowser keeps favourites in a storage container and posters on the cache drive. Both work under xenia-edge with the storage fixes in the pr-silverlight-exports pull request (see Status under xenia ).

docs.text: Testing in xenia ¶ tools\Test-XboxApp.ps1 runs a built app in xenia, presses controller buttons at set times, takes screenshots of the xenia window and checks the log: .\tools\Test-XboxApp.ps1 -Xex .\samples\ui\FocusNavigation\bin\Release\xbox\default.xex ` -Output $env:TEMP\focus-test ` -Steps '14:shot','15:DPadRight','16:DPadDown','17:A','18:shot' -Seconds 20 Each step is <second>:<button> or <second>:shot . At the end it prints: LastFrame The last frame number in the log. A low number means the app stalled. Crashed Whether the guest crashed. MissingExports Kernel or XAM functions the app called that xenia doesn't implement. Log The path to the full log. Buttons are sent as key messages to the xenia window only, so nothing reaches other windows. xenia runs with its keyboard input driver, and the D-pad, A and B are rebound to numpad keys. xenia's defaults for those need Shift or depend on the keyboard layout, which can't be sent to one window. Button Key Button Key A numpad 5 DPadUp/Down/Left/Right numpad 8/2/4/6 B numpad 0 LeftStickUp/Down/Left/Right W/S/A/D X L LeftShoulder, RightShoulder 1, 3 Y P LeftTrigger, RightTrigger Q, E Start X Back Z Apps need about 12 seconds to show their first page in xenia. Start pressing buttons after that. The script runs the xenia_edge.exe given with -Xenia , else the one in the XENIA_EDGE environment variable, else the one on PATH . -ExtraArgs passes more xenia options. Debug output ¶ System.Diagnostics.Debug.WriteLine , Debugger.Log and Console.WriteLine don't throw, but their output goes nowhere: the CLR only passes debug output to an attached managed debugger. To log from C#, call the kernel's DbgPrint instead. samples\Common\DebugLog.cs wraps it: DebugLog.WriteLine("Loaded {0} items", items.Count); xenia writes each line to its log as (DbgPrint) Loaded 12 items ; a development kit shows it in its debug output. The text is passed as an argument to a %s format, so a % in it is printed as is. HelloXbox logs its start this way, and MediaPlayer logs every state change and failure.

docs.text: tools\Test-XboxApp.ps1 runs a built app in xenia, presses controller buttons at set times, takes screenshots of the xenia window and checks the log: .\tools\Test-XboxApp.ps1 -Xex .\samples\ui\FocusNavigation\bin\Release\xbox\default.xex ` -Output $env:TEMP\focus-test ` -Steps '14:shot','15:DPadRight','16:DPadDown','17:A','18:shot' -Seconds 20 Each step is <second>:<button> or <second>:shot . At the end it prints: LastFrame The last frame number in the log. A low number means the app stalled. Crashed Whether the guest crashed. MissingExports Kernel or XAM functions the app called that xenia doesn't implement. Log The path to the full log. Buttons are sent as key messages to the xenia window only, so nothing reaches other windows. xenia runs with its keyboard input driver, and the D-pad, A and B are rebound to numpad keys. xenia's defaults for those need Shift or depend on the keyboard layout, which can't be sent to one window. Button Key Button Key A numpad 5 DPadUp/Down/Left/Right numpad 8/2/4/6 B numpad 0 LeftStickUp/Down/Left/Right W/S/A/D X L LeftShoulder, RightShoulder 1, 3 Y P LeftTrigger, RightTrigger Q, E Start X Back Z Apps need about 12 seconds to show their first page in xenia. Start pressing buttons after that. The script runs the xenia_edge.exe given with -Xenia , else the one in the XENIA_EDGE environment variable, else the one on PATH . -ExtraArgs passes more xenia options.

docs.text: Status under xenia ¶ Silverlight apps need xenia-edge plus three pull requests that aren't merged yet: Pull request What it adds #325 What apps need to start: locale, guest timers and mutants, XamContentOpenFile . #326 XHttp over the host's HTTP client: every WebClient and HttpWebRequest . #327 The exports apps call once running, and a second commit that fixes XNA storage containers, the cache drive and MediaTransport commands. The samples were tested on a build of xenia-edge with all three merged. Works ¶ Tested with XAML UI, layout, styles, templates, visual states every sample Controller input: buttons, sticks, triggers GamepadInput Focus, A clicking buttons, DirectionalFocus FocusNavigation Pivot with grid navigation, Rune , Legend XboxControls XboxApplicationFrame , pages, transitions, back navigation PageNavigation HTTP GET and POST, XML, images from the network HelloXbox, CatalogBrowser Signed-in gamer, gamertag CatalogBrowser Storage containers (encrypted files) PlatformCalls, CatalogBrowser Cache container PlatformCalls, CatalogBrowser MediaTransport and its transport bar PlatformCalls, MediaPlayer DllImport into xam and the kernel NativeProbe Doesn't work yet ¶ Media playback WMA plays. WMV and MP3 play with a xenia-edge build that loads the console's extra AV codec module ( dash.ExtraAVCodecs.xex in xenia's system\ folder); that loader is pull request #329 , not merged yet. MP4 also needs the Optional Media Update and plays with a garbled picture (unsupported k_32 texture format). See Media . SmartGlass keyboard Opening a Rune calls XamLrcKeyboardRegister and related functions, which xenia doesn't have. The Rune still works with the controller. System screens Most Guide screens (friends, gamer card, ...) aren't implemented in xenia. Xbox LIVE and XAuth No tokens, so sign-in to partner services, Marketplace and social networks fails. Kinect and speech xenia has no Kinect. The donor title ¶ A package runs as the donor app (the window title shows 574407D1 Plex with the default profile), with the donor's title ID and save area. xenia applies the donor's installed title update to the runtime's native images if one is installed; that's harmless, and the log mentions it.

docs.text: class Microsoft.Xbox.Controls.Primitives.ResolutionNormalizingPanel A panel that lays out its children at a fixed logical height and scales them to the panel's actual size, so content designed for one resolution looks the same at 720p and 1080p. docs.text: class Microsoft.Xbox.Controls.Primitives.TipsManager Shows Kinect tips and the wave-to-engage progress in the Feedback strip. While loaded, the control listens to the Kinect sensor: it shows a warming-up tip while the sensor starts, an identifying tip and a welcome message (with the user's gamertag when known) when a user engages, and the left- or right-hand wave progress. If the VuiBar is enabled and recognizing, a voice tip is shown every 30 seconds. Most tips fade after 10 seconds. The text properties are set by the control from its localized strings and are refreshed when Localization.Culture changes, so values you assign may be overwritten. docs.text: class Microsoft.Xbox.Controls.Primitives.VirtualizingGrid The paging items panel of ContinuousList . It places item containers into a Grid column by column and only keeps the columns around the visible page realized. Use it only as the items panel of a ContinuousList ; it reports paging and visible items back to that list. Items fill the grid's rows top to bottom, then move to the next column. MediaElementAdapterState ¶ enum Microsoft.Xbox.Controls.MediaElementAdapterState The playback states reported by an IMediaElementAdapter . Values Busy The player is buffering, acquiring a license or otherwise not ready to play; the transport shows its busy indicator. Closed No media is open, or media is still opening. Paused Playback is paused. Playing Media is playing. Stopped Playback is stopped. MediaTransport ¶ class Microsoft.Xbox.Controls.MediaTransport Full-screen video playback chrome for Xbox: an overlay with a NUI timeline, a controller transport bar, status text, a busy indicator and an optional custom control panel, wired to a media player. Put a MediaElement , a Smooth Streaming SmoothStreamingMediaElement or your own IMediaElementAdapter in Content (it is assigned to MediaTransport.MediaElement automatically), or set MediaTransport.MediaElement directly. While loaded, the transport polls the player every 100 ms and updates MediaTransport.Position , MediaTransport.Duration , the seekable range, MediaTransport.PlayRate , MediaTransport.IsBusy and the automatic button states. Input: A, Start, Enter or the D-pad show the transport bar with focus on Play/Pause; the triggers rewind and fast forward; the shoulder buttons skip to the previous/next chapter marker; B hides the bar, panel or overlay, and raises MediaTransport.Back when nothing is left to hide; the Back button always raises MediaTransport.Back . Remote media keys are routed through MediaTransport.ExecuteMediaCommand . With Kinect, an engaged user sees the overlay and can scrub the timeline with the hand gesture handled by NuiTimeline . Fast forward and rewind are emulated: the player is paused and the timeline position advances at the selected PlayRate ; the player is seeked to the previewed position when the user plays or pauses. Side effects while loaded and enabled: the console is told that video is playing (native ordinal 602) so the dashboard treats the app as a media app; the media state (position, duration, rate, capabilities and MediaTransport.MediaAssetId ) is reported for companion devices (native ordinal 600); the screen saver is suppressed during playback when MediaTransport.IsScreenSaverAutoDisabled is set (requires GamerServices to be initialized, which XboxApplicationFrame does); and play, pause, stop, skip and scrub actions are reported to the media usage service. Important: the usage reporting requires MediaTransport.MediaAssetId . Play, Pause, Stop, skip, scrubbing, Back and rate changes throw InvalidOperationException if it is null or empty, so set it before playback starts. Methods System.Void AddDefaultVuiBarCommands() Adds the standard media voice commands to the VuiBar . Adds Play, Pause and Stop to VuiBar.PrimaryCommands and Fast Forward, Rewind, Slower and Faster to VuiBar.SecondaryCommands , skipping any already present. The transport handles these commands while it is loaded and enables or disables them to match its state. Throws InvalidOperationException if no VuiBar exists. System.Void ExecuteMediaCommand(System.Windows.Media.MediaCommand command) Carries out a media command as if the user had pressed the corresponding button. Commands whose Is…Enabled property is false are ignored. After a command runs, the overlay is shown with a status message, MediaTransport.MediaCommandExecuted is raised and the media state is reported to companion devices. Fast forward and rewind step through the PlayRate values (2x up to 128x) on each call. PreviousTrack and NextTrack seek to the previous/next ChapterMarker (or the start/end of the seekable range) and play. Play, Pause, Stop and skip commands require MediaTransport.MediaAssetId . System.Void HideCustomControlPanel() Hides the custom control panel, if MediaTransport.IsCustomControlPanelEnabled is true . System.Void HideOverlay() Hides the overlay and cancels any keep-visible request. Also hides the status area unless it was shown with auto-hide disabled. System.Void HideStatus() Hides the status area and cancels any keep-visible request. System.Void HideTransportBar() Hides the transport bar and cancels any keep-visible request from MediaTransport.ShowTransportBar . If focus was in the bar, it moves to the transport itself. System.Void OnApplyTemplate() System.Void OnContentChanged(System.Object oldContent, System.Object newContent) Called when Content changes; assigns supported player objects to MediaTransport.MediaElement . System.Void RemoveDefaultVuiBarCommands() Removes the standard media voice commands added by MediaTransport.AddDefaultVuiBarCommands from the VuiBar . Throws InvalidOperationException if no VuiBar exists. Call it when leaving the playback page so the commands do not stay on the voice bar. System.Void Seek(System.TimeSpan newPosition) Seeks the player to a new position. Does nothing if there is no player, the media is closed, the player cannot seek, or it is already at that position. Cancels any fast forward or rewind and raises MediaTransport.SeekExecuted . System.Void SeekToLive() Seeks a live stream to its live edge and starts playing. Does nothing unless the player is open, can seek and reports live content. Raises MediaTransport.SeekExecuted with SeekExecutedEventArgs.IsToLive set. Microsoft.Xbox.Controls.NuiScrollViewer A vertically scrolling content area designed for both the controller and the Kinect hand cursor. With the controller, holding D-pad up/down or pushing the left stick past 75% scrolls smoothly, starting slowly and accelerating. The key press is marked handled only when there is room to scroll in that direction, so focus can leave the viewer at the ends. With Kinect, hovering the hand cursor over the viewer for 300 ms gives it focus, and while the cursor is over the upper three eighths or lower three eighths of the viewer the content scrolls up or down. SwipeViewer ¶ class Microsoft.Xbox.Controls.SwipeViewer Detects Kinect left and right swipe gestures and exposes their progress as events, properties and visual states. The gesture is recognized by the console (npctrl.dll ordinals 300–305); the viewer configures two activation zones and receives callbacks on the UI thread. Without a Kinect sensor or an engaged user, no events are raised. Only one SwipeViewer can be active at a time. A viewer becomes active when it is loaded, enabled and (inside an XboxApplicationFrame ) on the current page; activating a second one throws InvalidOperationException . Pivot and ContinuousList each contain one, so don't place two such controls on the same page, and disable a viewer ( IsEnabled = false ) before showing another. Sequence: SwipeViewer.PeekStarted , then SwipeViewer.PeekProgressChanged as the hand moves into a zone, SwipeViewer.PeekCompleted at full peek, SwipeViewer.SwipeReady , and finally SwipeViewer.SwipeCompleted or SwipeViewer.SwipeFailed . The bar itself is not a tab stop. D-pad (or left stick) left/right move focus between enabled, visible buttons and wrap around at the ends. When a button gets focus its TransportBarButton.StatusText is copied to TransportBar.CurrentStatusText . If no enabled button has that command, the first enabled button gets focus. VuiBar ¶ class Microsoft.Xbox.Controls.VuiBar The voice user interface (VUI) bar: Kinect speech recognition for the app and the on-screen bar that lists the commands the user can say. Only one instance can exist; it is available as VuiBar.Current . The default XboxApplicationFrame template already contains it, so apps normally do not create one. Creating a second instance throws InvalidOperationException . Typical setup: create one or more VuiGrammar objects with phrases whose semantic values match your commands' VuiCommand.SemanticValue , call VuiBar.LoadGrammar for each, add VuiCommand objects to VuiBar.PrimaryCommands or VuiBar.SecondaryCommands , and call VuiBar.StartRecognition . Grammars can only be loaded or unloaded while recognition is stopped. The phrases for the built-in VuiCommands are loaded automatically. The user says "Xbox" to open the bar (active listening, which times out after 12 seconds without a command). While the bar is open the user can say a command phrase on its own; while it is closed, a command can be said together with the "Xbox" keyword. The two cases use separate confidence thresholds. If a phrase matches several executable commands the bar enters disambiguation and labels the candidates (see VuiBar.SetDisambiguationSlots ). Commands with a VuiCommand.Confirmation ask for confirmation before running. Two fixed commands, Cancel and go Home (with an explicit confirmation), are always available while the bar is open. Speech requires a Kinect sensor, a supported Localization.Culture and speech recognition being enabled in the console settings; check VuiBar.IsCurrentCultureSupported and VuiBar.IsDashSpeechRecognitionEnabled . Changing Localization.Culture stops recognition and unloads all grammars, including the app's. Events and command execution happen on the UI thread. Native calls go to npctrl.dll ordinals 200–218 and 1200. Constructors VuiBar() Properties Microsoft.Xbox.Controls.VuiBarVisibilityState VisibilityState { get; } Gets how the bar is currently displayed. Changes raise VisibilityStateChanged . MediaTransport uses this to make room for the bar. System.Boolean IsActiveListening { get; } Gets whether the bar is open and actively listening for commands. Changes raise VuiBar.ActiveListeningChanged . System.Boolean IsCurrentCultureSupported { get; } Gets whether speech recognition supports the current Localization.Culture . System.Boolean IsDashSpeechRecognitionEnabled { get; } Gets whether the user has speech recognition enabled in the console settings. System.Boolean IsEnabled { get; set; } Gets or sets whether speech recognition is enabled. Setting true while the culture is unsupported throws InvalidOperationException ; the value is ignored when speech is disabled in the console settings. Disabling the bar pauses the recognizer and dismisses any open bar, confirmation or disambiguation. System.Boolean IsRecognitionStarted { get; } Gets whether VuiBar.StartRecognition has been called (and VuiBar.StopRecognition has not). System.Collections.Generic.IList<Microsoft.Xbox.Controls.VuiCommand> ConfirmationCommands { get; } Gets the commands currently offered to confirm or cancel a command. System.Collections.Generic.IList<Microsoft.Xbox.Controls.VuiCommand> ExecutablePrimaryCommands { get; } Gets the subset of VuiBar.PrimaryCommands that can currently execute, in the same order. System.Collections.Generic.IList<Microsoft.Xbox.Controls.VuiCommand> ExecutableSecondaryCommands { get; } Gets the subset of VuiBar.SecondaryCommands that can currently execute, in the same order. System.Collections.Generic.IList<Microsoft.Xbox.Controls.VuiCommand> FixedCommands { get; } Gets the built-in commands that are always available while the bar is open (Cancel and go Home). System.Collections.Generic.IList<Microsoft.Xbox.Controls.VuiCommand> PrimaryCommands { get; } Gets the commands shown prominently on the bar. Adding a command throws InvalidOperationException if it is null , has no VuiCommand.DisplayText or VuiCommand.SemanticValue , needs confirmation but has no VuiCommand.ConfirmationText , is a fixed command, is already on the bar, or shares a semantic value with a command already on the bar. If no loaded grammar contains its semantic value, VuiBar.VuiCommandNotRecognized is raised with VuiCommandNotRecognizedReason.PhraseNotLoaded . System.Collections.Generic.IList<Microsoft.Xbox.Controls.VuiCommand> SecondaryCommands { get; } Gets the less prominent commands shown on the bar. static Microsoft.Xbox.Controls.VuiBar Current { get; } Gets the app's single VuiBar instance. Methods System.Void LoadGrammar(Microsoft.Xbox.Controls.VuiGrammar grammar) Loads a grammar into the speech recognizer so its phrases can be recognized. Throws InvalidOperationException if recognition is started, the grammar is already loaded or it has no phrases. After loading, VuiGrammar.IsLoaded is true and no more phrases can be added. Phrases become active only while a command with the same semantic value is on the bar and can execute. All grammars are unloaded automatically when Localization.Culture changes. System.Void OnApplyTemplate() System.Void SetDisambiguationSlots(System.Collections.Generic.IEnumerable<Microsoft.Xbox.Controls.VuiDisambiguationSlot> slots) Sets the labels used to tell apart commands that match the same phrase. When disambiguation starts, executable commands that have a UI element and VuiCommand.IsDisambiguationEnabled set are assigned slots in order, and each slot's VuiDisambiguationSlot.DisambiguationText is shown as the command's VuiCommand.DisambiguationText . The slot semantic values must match phrases in a loaded grammar. Throws ArgumentException if a slot has empty text or semantic value, or if fewer than VuiBar.MinDisambiguationSlotCount slots are given. System.Void StartRecognition() Starts listening for speech. The recognizer is started on the next dispatcher cycle, and only if the bar is enabled; if the bar is disabled it starts when the bar is enabled. Calling this while already started does nothing. Load your grammars first, because grammars cannot be loaded while recognition is started. System.Void StopRecognition() Stops listening for speech. Call this before loading or unloading grammars. Does nothing if recognition is not started. System.Void UnloadGrammar(Microsoft.Xbox.Controls.VuiGrammar grammar) Removes a loaded grammar from the speech recognizer. Throws ArgumentNullException if grammar is null , and InvalidOperationException if recognition is started. Its phrases cannot be added to again after unloading; create a new grammar instead. Events event System.EventHandler<Microsoft.Xbox.Controls.VuiActiveListeningChangedEventArgs> ActiveListeningChanged Occurs when VuiBar.IsActiveListening changes. Pivot uses this to highlight page headers that can be spoken. event System.EventHandler<Microsoft.Xbox.Controls.VuiBarVisibilityStateChangedEventArgs> VisibilityStateChanged event System.EventHandler<Microsoft.Xbox.Controls.VuiCommandNotRecognizedEventArgs> VuiCommandNotRecognized Occurs when speech was heard but did not run a command, or when a command is added whose phrase is not loaded. Use it for diagnostics or to give the user feedback. See VuiCommandNotRecognizedReason for the possible causes. The property itself is not public; bind to it from a custom VuiBar template. static System.Windows.DependencyProperty DisambiguationTextProperty Identifies the read-only DisambiguationText dependency property: the localized prompt shown while the user must choose between matching commands. The property itself is not public; bind to it from a custom VuiBar template. static System.Windows.DependencyProperty IsActiveListeningProperty static System.Windows.DependencyProperty IsRecognitionStartedProperty static System.Windows.DependencyProperty ListeningTextProperty Identifies the read-only ListeningText dependency property: the localized prompt the bar shows while listening with no commands to list. The property itself is not public; bind to it from a custom VuiBar template. static System.Windows.DependencyProperty VisibilityStateProperty static System.Windows.DependencyProperty VuiLanguageProperty Identifies the read-only VuiLanguage dependency property: the speech language selected from the current culture (US English by default). The property itself is not public. VuiBarVisibilityState ¶ enum Microsoft.Xbox.Controls.VuiBarVisibilityState How the VuiBar is displayed. Values Hidden The bar is not shown. Shown The bar is shown at its normal size (listening or confirming). ShownLarge The bar is shown enlarged, while disambiguating between commands with primary commands present. VuiBarVisibilityStateChangedEventArgs ¶ class Microsoft.Xbox.Controls.VuiBarVisibilityStateChangedEventArgs Provides data for the VisibilityStateChanged event of VuiBar . Properties Microsoft.Xbox.Controls.VuiBarVisibilityState VisibilityState { get; } Gets the new visibility state of the bar. VuiCommand ¶ class Microsoft.Xbox.Controls.VuiCommand A command the user can trigger by voice through the VuiBar . A command is matched to speech through its VuiCommand.SemanticValue : load a VuiGrammar containing one or more phrases with that semantic value, then add the command to VuiBar.PrimaryCommands or VuiBar.SecondaryCommands (or assign it to PivotItem.VuiCommand ). When recognized, the command runs VuiCommand.TargetCommand and raises VuiCommand.Executed . The command is an ICommand , so it can also be bound to buttons. A command can be attached to only one loaded UI element at a time; doing otherwise throws InvalidOperationException . The predefined commands in VuiCommands are built in: their display text, semantic value and confirmation settings cannot be changed. Constructors VuiCommand() Properties Microsoft.Xbox.Controls.VuiConfirmation Confirmation { get; set; } Gets or sets whether the user must confirm the command before it runs. Requires VuiCommand.ConfirmationText when not VuiConfirmation.None . Throws InvalidOperationException for built-in commands. Microsoft.Xbox.Controls.VuiPersistence Persistence { get; set; } Gets or sets what happens to the bar's active listening after the command executes. System.Boolean IsBuiltIn { get; } Gets whether the command is one of the predefined commands in VuiCommands (or an internal confirmation command). System.Boolean IsDisambiguationEnabled { get; set; } Gets or sets whether the command may be offered as a candidate when several commands match a phrase. Only commands attached to a Button take part in disambiguation. System.Boolean IsEnabled { get; set; } Gets or sets whether the command may execute. Disabled commands are removed from the executable lists and their phrases are deactivated. MediaTransport and Pivot manage this property for the commands they own. System.Boolean IsFixed { get; } Gets whether the command is one of the bar's fixed commands (Cancel, go Home). System.Object TargetCommandParameter { get; set; } Gets or sets the parameter passed to VuiCommand.TargetCommand . System.String ConfirmationText { get; set; } Gets or sets the question or notice shown while the command is being confirmed. Throws InvalidOperationException for built-in commands. System.String DisambiguationText { get; } Gets the label assigned to the command while the bar is disambiguating between matching commands. System.String DisplayText { get; set; } Gets or sets the text shown for the command on the bar. Throws InvalidOperationException for built-in commands, whose text is localized automatically. Show the words the user should say. System.String SemanticValue { get; set; } Gets or sets the value that links the command to grammar phrases. Throws InvalidOperationException for built-in commands and while the command is on the bar. The value must be unique among commands on the bar and must not be "xbox" or a built-in semantic value. System.Windows.Input.ICommand TargetCommand { get; set; } Gets or sets an ICommand to run when the voice command executes. The voice command can execute only while the target's CanExecute returns true for VuiCommand.TargetCommandParameter ; its CanExecuteChanged is tracked. Methods System.Boolean CanExecute(System.Object parameter) Determines whether the command can execute. System.Void Execute(System.Object parameter) Executes the command: runs VuiCommand.TargetCommand and raises VuiCommand.Executed . Must be called on the UI thread. Throws InvalidOperationException if VuiCommand.CanExecute returns false . Re-entrant calls while the command is executing are ignored. Events event System.EventHandler<Microsoft.Xbox.Controls.VuiCommandExecutedEventArgs> Executed Occurs after the command has executed (after VuiCommand.TargetCommand has run). Raised on the UI thread. The built-in commands in VuiCommands are static, so remove handlers you add to them when your page unloads. VuiCommandExecutedEventArgs ¶ class Microsoft.Xbox.Controls.VuiCommandExecutedEventArgs Provides data for the VuiCommand.Executed event. It carries no additional information. Constructors VuiCommandExecutedEventArgs() VuiCommandNotRecognizedEventArgs ¶ class Microsoft.Xbox.Controls.VuiCommandNotRecognizedEventArgs Provides data for the VuiBar.VuiCommandNotRecognized event. Properties Microsoft.Xbox.Controls.VuiCommand VuiCommand { get; } Gets the command involved, if one was found; otherwise null . Microsoft.Xbox.Controls.VuiCommandNotRecognizedReason Reason { get; } Gets why no command was executed. System.Double Confidence { get; } Gets the recognizer's confidence in the phrase, from 0 to 1. System.Double RequiredConfidence { get; } Gets the confidence that would have been required, for the confidence-related reasons; otherwise 0. System.String SemanticValue { get; } Gets the semantic value of the recognized phrase (or of the command, for VuiCommandNotRecognizedReason.PhraseNotLoaded ). System.String Text { get; } Gets the recognized phrase text, or null for VuiCommandNotRecognizedReason.PhraseNotLoaded . VuiCommandNotRecognizedReason ¶ enum Microsoft.Xbox.Controls.VuiCommandNotRecognizedReason Explains why VuiBar.VuiCommandNotRecognized was raised. Values LanguageActiveConfidence The phrase was spoken on its own while the bar was open but its confidence was below the speech language's default threshold. LanguageNormalConfidence The phrase was spoken with the "Xbox" keyword but its confidence was below the speech language's default threshold. None No reason given. PhraseActiveConfidence The phrase was spoken on its own while the bar was open but its confidence was below the phrase's own threshold. PhraseNormalConfidence The phrase was spoken with the "Xbox" keyword but its confidence was below the phrase's own threshold. PhraseNotFound The recognizer returned a rule that does not belong to any loaded phrase. PhraseNotLoaded A command was added to the bar but no loaded grammar contains a phrase with its semantic value, so it can never be spoken. TargetCommandCannotExecute The matching command is enabled but its VuiCommand.TargetCommand cannot execute. VuiCommandDisabled The matching command's VuiCommand.IsEnabled is false . VuiCommandNotFound The phrase was recognized but no command on the bar has its semantic value. WaitingForSelectionAnimation Speech arrived while a previously recognized command was still playing its selection animation. XboxConfidence The "Xbox" keyword spoken with the phrase was recognized with too little confidence. VuiCommands ¶ class Microsoft.Xbox.Controls.VuiCommands Predefined, localized voice commands for common actions. The phrases for these commands are loaded automatically for the current speech language, so you only need to add the commands to the VuiBar and handle VuiCommand.Executed or set VuiCommand.TargetCommand . Their display text and semantic values cannot be changed. The instances are shared app-wide. MediaTransport.AddDefaultVuiBarCommands adds the media commands for you. Properties static Microsoft.Xbox.Controls.VuiCommand FastForward { get; } Gets the built-in "Fast Forward" command. static Microsoft.Xbox.Controls.VuiCommand Faster { get; } Gets the built-in "Faster" command. static Microsoft.Xbox.Controls.VuiCommand GoBack { get; } Gets the built-in "Go Back" command. static Microsoft.Xbox.Controls.VuiCommand Next { get; } Gets the built-in "Next" command. static Microsoft.Xbox.Controls.VuiCommand No { get; } Gets the built-in "No" command. static Microsoft.Xbox.Controls.VuiCommand Pause { get; } Gets the built-in "Pause" command. For US English this command accepts a lower recognition confidence while the bar is open. static Microsoft.Xbox.Controls.VuiCommand Play { get; } Gets the built-in "Play" command. static Microsoft.Xbox.Controls.VuiCommand Previous { get; } Gets the built-in "Previous" command. static Microsoft.Xbox.Controls.VuiCommand Rewind { get; } Gets the built-in "Rewind" command. static Microsoft.Xbox.Controls.VuiCommand Slower { get; } Gets the built-in "Slower" command. static Microsoft.Xbox.Controls.VuiCommand Stop { get; } Gets the built-in "Stop" command. static Microsoft.Xbox.Controls.VuiCommand Yes { get; } Gets the built-in "Yes" command. The bar uses its own copies of Yes and No for confirmations; this instance is for app use. VuiConfirmation ¶ enum Microsoft.Xbox.Controls.VuiConfirmation Specifies whether a VuiCommand must be confirmed before it runs. Values Explicit The bar shows the confirmation text and runs the command only if the user says Yes within 5 seconds; No or a timeout cancels it. Implicit The bar shows the confirmation text and runs the command after 3 seconds unless the user says Cancel. None The command runs immediately when recognized. VuiDisambiguationSlot ¶ class Microsoft.Xbox.Controls.VuiDisambiguationSlot A label used by the VuiBar to let the user pick one of several commands that matched the same phrase. Pass a list of slots to VuiBar.SetDisambiguationSlots , and load a grammar with a phrase for each slot's semantic value. Constructors VuiDisambiguationSlot(System.String disambiguationText, System.String disambiguationSemanticValue) Initializes a new disambiguation slot. Properties System.String DisambiguationSemanticValue { get; } Gets the semantic value of the phrase that selects this slot. System.String DisambiguationText { get; } Gets the label shown next to a candidate command (for example a number the user can say). VuiGrammar ¶ class Microsoft.Xbox.Controls.VuiGrammar A set of spoken phrases, each mapped to a semantic value, that can be loaded into the VuiBar recognizer. Add phrases with VuiGrammar.AddPhrase and then call VuiBar.LoadGrammar while recognition is stopped. Several phrases may share a semantic value (synonyms). A phrase is active only while a VuiCommand with the same semantic value is on the bar and can execute. Phrases should be in the language of the current culture. Constructors VuiGrammar() Properties System.Boolean IsLoaded { get; } Gets whether the grammar is loaded into the recognizer. Methods System.Void AddPhrase(System.String text, System.String semanticValue) Adds a phrase that uses the speech language's default confidence thresholds. Same rules as VuiGrammar.AddPhrase . System.Void AddPhrase(System.String text, System.String semanticValue, System.Double normalRequiredConfidence, System.Double activeRequiredConfidence) Adds a phrase with its own recognition confidence thresholds. Throws InvalidOperationException if the grammar is loaded, ArgumentException for invalid text or semantic values, and ArgumentOutOfRangeException for confidences outside 0–1. VuiPersistence ¶ enum Microsoft.Xbox.Controls.VuiPersistence Specifies whether the VuiBar keeps actively listening after a command executes. Values Dismiss Close the bar after the command runs. ForceMaintain Open the bar (or keep it open) after the command runs, with the 12-second listening timeout. ForceMaintainNoTimeout Open the bar (or keep it open) after the command runs, with no timeout. Maintain Keep the bar open if it was already open, restarting the 12-second listening timeout. XboxApplicationFrame ¶ class Microsoft.Xbox.Controls.XboxApplicationFrame The navigation frame to use as the root of an Xbox Silverlight app. It hosts pages, plays page transitions and contains the app's VuiBar . Creating the frame initializes GamerServices ( GamerServicesDispatcher.Initialize ) and the UI sound system if they are not initialized yet, and pumps the XNA framework and GamerServices dispatchers on every rendered frame. Controls that depend on GamerServices, such as the screen-saver handling in MediaTransport , therefore work automatically inside this frame. The template must contain a VuiBar named PART_VuiBar (the default template does); otherwise InvalidOperationException is thrown. Only one VuiBar may exist per app, so do not add another one when you use this frame. On navigation the old and new pages are shown in two presenters and their navigation transitions (set with the TransitionService attached properties) are played. Elements marked as transition targets animate in order after the page. Any SwipeViewer on the outgoing page is turned off and the one on the incoming page is turned on. Constructors XboxApplicationFrame() Methods System.Void OnApplyTemplate() System.Void OnContentChanged(System.Object oldContent, System.Object newContent) Starts the page transition when the frame's content changes. Completes any transition still in progress, places both pages in the frame's presenters, and starts the out and in transitions once the new page's items controls have loaded (or after 0.3 seconds if it has none). XboxApplicationPage ¶ class Microsoft.Xbox.Controls.XboxApplicationPage A Page preconfigured with Z-order navigation transitions so that pages layer correctly while XboxApplicationFrame animates between them. Replace the page's TransitionService navigation transitions if you want a different animation. Constructors XboxApplicationPage()
