docs.text: class Microsoft.Xbox.Controls.ContinuousList A horizontally paged list for the 10-foot UI. Items are laid out in columns and the user pages left and right with the shoulder buttons, the D-pad, the remote's previous/next keys or a Kinect swipe. Items are wrapped in ContinuousListItem containers and arranged by a VirtualizingGrid items panel (the default template). The number of rows comes from the row definitions of the panel's VirtualizingGrid.Grid ; columns are created as needed. The template contains a SwipeViewer named SwipeElement , so the list responds to Kinect swipes. Only one SwipeViewer can be active at a time, so do not show two swipe-enabled controls (for example a ContinuousList and a Pivot ) on the same page. Raises ItemsInViewChanged whenever the set of fully visible items changes. During page transitions in an XboxApplicationFrame the item area is clipped to the screen. Constructors ContinuousList() Properties System.Boolean CanGoToNextPage { get; } Gets whether there is a page to the right of the current one. System.Boolean CanGoToPreviousPage { get; } Gets whether there is a page to the left of the current one. System.Boolean IsCascadeAnimationEnabled { get; set; } Gets or sets whether items animate in one column after another when the list is loaded or its items source changes. System.Collections.ObjectModel.ReadOnlyCollection<System.Object> ItemsInView { get; } Gets the items that are currently inside the view area. System.Double PageAlignment { get; set; } Gets or sets the horizontal offset, in pixels, at which the first column of a page is placed. The space between this offset and the left edge of ContinuousList.ViewMargin is where the previous page peeks in. System.TimeSpan CascadeAnimationBeginTime { get; set; } Gets or sets the delay before the cascade animation starts. Set the attached properties ( AButtonText , BButtonText , XButtonText , YButtonText ) on a control. docs.text: class Microsoft.Xbox.Controls.MediaTransport Full-screen video playback chrome for Xbox: an overlay with a NUI timeline, a controller transport bar, status text, a busy indicator and an optional custom control panel, wired to a media player. Put a MediaElement , a Smooth Streaming SmoothStreamingMediaElement or your own IMediaElementAdapter in Content (it is assigned to MediaTransport.MediaElement automatically), or set MediaTransport.MediaElement directly. While loaded, the transport polls the player every 100 ms and updates MediaTransport.Position , MediaTransport.Duration , the seekable range, MediaTransport.PlayRate , MediaTransport.IsBusy and the automatic button states. Input: A, Start, Enter or the D-pad show the transport bar with focus on Play/Pause; the triggers rewind and fast forward; the shoulder buttons skip to the previous/next chapter marker; B hides the bar, panel or overlay, and raises MediaTransport.Back when nothing is left to hide; the Back button always raises MediaTransport.Back . Remote media keys are routed through MediaTransport.ExecuteMediaCommand . With Kinect, an engaged user sees the overlay and can scrub the timeline with the hand gesture handled by NuiTimeline . Fast forward and rewind are emulated: the player is paused and the timeline position advances at the selected PlayRate ; the player is seeked to the previewed position when the user plays or pauses. Side effects while loaded and enabled: the console is told that video is playing (native ordinal 602) so the dashboard treats the app as a media app; the media state (position, duration, rate, capabilities and MediaTransport.MediaAssetId ) is reported for companion devices (native ordinal 600); the screen saver is suppressed during playback when MediaTransport.IsScreenSaverAutoDisabled is set (requires GamerServices to be initialized, which XboxApplicationFrame does); and play, pause, stop, skip and scrub actions are reported to the media usage service. Important: the usage reporting requires MediaTransport.MediaAssetId . Play, Pause, Stop, skip, scrubbing, Back and rate changes throw InvalidOperationException if it is null or empty, so set it before playback starts. Constructors MediaTransport() Properties Microsoft.Xbox.Controls.LeftButtonMode LeftButtonMode { get; set; } Gets or sets which button is shown on the left of the overlay. Microsoft.Xbox.Controls.NuiTimeline NuiTimeline { get; } Gets the NuiTimeline template part named NuiTimeline . Microsoft.Xbox.Controls.PlayRate PlayRate { get; } Gets the current playback rate. Changes raise PlayRateChanged and update the play/pause button and voice commands. Microsoft.Xbox.Controls.SignalStrengthMode SignalStrengthMode { get; set; } Gets or sets the signal-strength indicator shown on the timeline. Microsoft.Xbox.Controls.TransportBar TransportBar { get; } Gets the TransportBar template part named TransportBar . While the voice bar is shown the panel's bottom margin is raised so it sits above the bar; the margin and transport bar are restored when the voice bar hides. System.Boolean IsAutoDisengageEnabled { get; set; } Gets or sets whether the engaged Kinect user is automatically disengaged during playback. When enabled, the user is force-disengaged 10 seconds after the overlay was last shown if the media is still playing, so the hand cursor does not stay over the video. System.Boolean IsBusy { get; } Gets whether the player is busy (buffering, opening a license and so on). System.Boolean IsCustomControlPanelEnabled { get; set; } Gets or sets whether the custom control panel is used. When enabled, the panel is shown together with the transport bar and the overlay, the D-pad up/down keys open the transport bar, and the panel can be shown with MediaTransport.ShowCustomControlPanel . Disabling it hides the panel. System.Boolean IsCustomControlPanelVisible { get; } Gets whether the custom control panel is visible. System.Boolean IsDisplayModeEnabled { get; set; } Gets or sets whether the Display command (cycle the video stretch mode) is available. System.Boolean IsDisplayModeVisible { get; set; } Gets or sets whether the Display Mode button is shown in the transport bar. System.Boolean IsFastForwardEnabled { get; set; } Gets or sets whether the Fast Forward command is available. Once you set this property it no longer follows the player. It also controls the Fast Forward and Faster voice commands. System.Boolean IsFastForwardVisible { get; set; } Gets or sets whether the Fast Forward button is shown in the transport bar. System.Boolean IsInfoEnabled { get; set; } Gets or sets whether the Info command (toggle the overlay) is available. System.Boolean IsInfoVisible { get; set; } Gets or sets whether the Info button is shown in the transport bar. System.Boolean IsLiveEnabled { get; set; } Gets or sets whether the Live command (jump to the live edge) is available. Once you set this property it no longer follows the player. System.Boolean IsLiveVisible { get; set; } Gets or sets whether the Live button is shown in the transport bar. System.Boolean IsNuiActive { get; } Gets whether the Kinect (NUI) controls are active. System.Boolean IsOverlayVisible { get; } Gets whether the overlay (timeline, Back/Stop and Play/Pause buttons) is visible. Raises IsOverlayVisibleChanged when it changes. System.Boolean IsPlayCountUsageEnabled { get; set; } Gets or sets whether media usage events are uploaded to the usage service. Even when disabled, the transport still requires MediaTransport.MediaAssetId for its usage bookkeeping. System.Boolean IsPlayPauseEnabled { get; set; } Gets or sets whether the Play and Pause commands are available. Once you set this property it no longer follows the player. It also controls the Play/Pause voice commands and is reported to companion devices. System.Boolean IsPlayPauseVisible { get; set; } Gets or sets whether the Play and Pause buttons are shown. System.Boolean IsProgressBarEnabled { get; set; } Gets or sets whether the timeline shows the playback progress bar. System.Boolean IsRewindEnabled { get; set; } Gets or sets whether the Rewind command is available. Once you set this property it no longer follows the player. It also controls the Rewind and Slower voice commands. System.Boolean IsRewindVisible { get; set; } Gets or sets whether the Rewind button is shown in the transport bar. System.Boolean IsScreenSaverAutoDisabled { get; set; } Gets or sets whether the console screen saver is suppressed while media plays. The screen saver is turned off while the transport is enabled, in the live tree and playing at normal speed, and restored otherwise. This uses Guide.IsScreenSaverEnabled and does nothing unless GamerServices has been initialized (as XboxApplicationFrame does). System.Boolean IsScrubbing { get; } Gets whether the user is currently scrubbing the timeline. System.Boolean IsScrubbingAllowed { get; } Gets whether timeline scrubbing is possible right now. System.Boolean IsScrubbingEnabled { get; set; } Gets or sets whether the user may scrub the timeline with Kinect. Scrubbing is actually possible only when MediaTransport.IsScrubbingAllowed is true . System.Boolean IsSkipBackEnabled { get; set; } Gets or sets whether the Skip Back (previous chapter) command is available. Once you set this property it no longer follows the player. System.Boolean IsSkipBackVisible { get; set; } Gets or sets whether the Skip Back button is shown in the transport bar. System.Boolean IsSkipForwardEnabled { get; set; } Gets or sets whether the Skip Forward (next chapter) command is available. Once you set this property it no longer follows the player. System.Boolean IsSkipForwardVisible { get; set; } Gets or sets whether the Skip Forward button is shown in the transport bar. System.Boolean IsStatusVisible { get; } Gets whether the status area is visible. System.Boolean IsStopEnabled { get; set; } Gets or sets whether the Stop command is available. Once you set this property it no longer follows the player state. It also controls the Stop voice command. System.Boolean IsStopVisible { get; set; } Gets or sets whether the Stop button is shown in the transport bar. System.Boolean IsThumbnailEnabled { get; set; } Gets or sets whether the timeline shows a preview thumbnail while scrubbing, fast forwarding or rewinding. Provide the thumbnail through MediaTransport.ThumbnailContent , typically in response to MediaTransport.ThumbnailRequest . System.Boolean IsTransportBarVisible { get; } Gets whether the controller transport bar is visible. The bar hides itself when the user switches to Kinect gestures. System.Collections.ObjectModel.ObservableCollection<Microsoft.Xbox.Controls.NuiTimelineMarker> Markers { get; } Gets the collection of markers displayed on the timeline. Add ChapterMarker objects to enable chapter skipping with the shoulder buttons and snapping while scrubbing. The transport raises MediaTransport.MarkerEntered and MediaTransport.MarkerExited as playback crosses markers. System.Collections.ObjectModel.ObservableCollection<Microsoft.Xbox.Controls.TransportBarButton> TransportBarButtons { get; } Gets the buttons displayed in the transport bar. When the transport loads, it inserts its built-in buttons at the front of the collection (Play, Pause, Skip Back, Rewind, Stop, Fast Forward, Skip Forward, Live, Info and Display Mode) and removes them again when it unloads or the culture changes. Add your own buttons after them. System.Double StatusContentWidth { get; } Gets the width available to the status area. System.Double ThumbnailAspectRatio { get; set; } Gets or sets the width-to-height ratio of the preview thumbnail. Once you set this property it no longer follows the control size. System.Object CustomControlPanelContent { get; set; } Gets or sets app-defined content shown in the custom control panel above the transport bar. The panel is used only when MediaTransport.IsCustomControlPanelEnabled is true . Focusable controls in it can be reached from the transport bar with the D-pad; if the content is replaced while it has focus, focus moves to its first focusable child or back to the transport. System.Object LowerOverlayContent { get; set; } Gets or sets app-defined content placed in the lower part of the overlay. System.Object MediaElement { get; set; } Gets or sets the player that the transport controls. Setting Content to one of the supported types sets this property for you. Adapters created internally for the built-in player types are disposed when the player is replaced; adapters you supply are not. The property is cleared when the transport is unloaded. System.Object StatusContent { get; set; } Gets or sets the content of the status area shown above the transport bar. The transport writes its own status text here (for example the play rate) when media commands run while the overlay is visible. System.Object ThumbnailContent { get; set; } Gets or sets the content shown in the timeline's preview thumbnail. Update it from a MediaTransport.ThumbnailRequest handler. System.Object UpperOverlayContent { get; set; } Gets or sets app-defined content placed in the upper part of the overlay. System.String EndPositionText { get; } Gets the formatted end position shown on the timeline. System.String MediaAssetId { get; set; } Gets or sets an identifier for the content being played, used for usage reporting and companion-device media state. Set this before playback starts: the transport's play, pause, stop, skip, scrub and Back handling throw InvalidOperationException when it is missing. Assigning a value reports a play event for the new asset and an end event for the previous one. IDs of 256 UTF-8 bytes or more are not passed to companion devices. System.String PositionText { get; } Gets the formatted current position shown on the timeline. System.TimeSpan Duration { get; set; } Gets or sets the length of the timeline. Once you set this property the transport stops updating it from the player. System.TimeSpan EndPosition { get; } Gets the media time shown at the right end of the timeline. System.TimeSpan MaximumPosition { get; set; } Gets or sets the latest position the user can seek or scrub to. Once you set this property the transport stops updating it from the player. Companion seek requests outside the minimum/maximum range are ignored. System.TimeSpan MinimumPosition { get; set; } Gets or sets the earliest position the user can seek or scrub to. Once you set this property the transport stops updating it from the player. Fast forward and rewind stop at this bound. System.TimeSpan Position { get; } Gets the current playback position. Changes update MediaTransport.PositionText , raise MediaTransport.MarkerEntered / MediaTransport.MarkerExited as markers are crossed, and raise MediaTransport.ThumbnailRequest while the timeline thumbnail is visible. Use MediaTransport.Seek to change the position. System.TimeSpan StartPosition { get; set; } Gets or sets the media time shown at the left end of the timeline. Once you set this property the transport stops updating it from the player. MediaTransport.EndPosition is recalculated. Adds Play, Pause and Stop to VuiBar.PrimaryCommands and Fast Forward, Rewind, Slower and Faster to VuiBar.SecondaryCommands , skipping any already present. The transport handles these commands while it is loaded and enables or disables them to match its state. Throws InvalidOperationException if no VuiBar exists. System.Void ExecuteMediaCommand(System.Windows.Media.MediaCommand command) Carries out a media command as if the user had pressed the corresponding button. Commands whose Is…Enabled property is false are ignored. After a command runs, the overlay is shown with a status message, MediaTransport.MediaCommandExecuted is raised and the media state is reported to companion devices. Fast forward and rewind step through the PlayRate values (2x up to 128x) on each call. PreviousTrack and NextTrack seek to the previous/next ChapterMarker (or the start/end of the seekable range) and play. Play, Pause, Stop and skip commands require MediaTransport.MediaAssetId . Cancels any fast forward or rewind and raises MediaTransport.SeekExecuted . System.Void SeekToLive() Seeks a live stream to its live edge and starts playing. Does nothing unless the player is open, can seek and reports live content. Raises MediaTransport.SeekExecuted with SeekExecutedEventArgs.IsToLive set. System.Void ShowCustomControlPanel(System.Boolean autoHide) Shows the custom control panel, if MediaTransport.IsCustomControlPanelEnabled is true . System.Void ShowOverlay(System.Boolean autoHide) Shows the overlay with the timeline and buttons. Also restarts the 10-second Kinect auto-disengage timer (see MediaTransport.IsAutoDisengageEnabled ). docs.text: class Microsoft.Xbox.Controls.NuiScrollViewer A vertically scrolling content area designed for both the controller and the Kinect hand cursor. With the controller, holding D-pad up/down or pushing the left stick past 75% scrolls smoothly, starting slowly and accelerating. The key press is marked handled only when there is room to scroll in that direction, so focus can leave the viewer at the ends. With Kinect, hovering the hand cursor over the viewer for 300 ms gives it focus, and while the cursor is over the upper three eighths or lower three eighths of the viewer the content scrolls up or down. Template parts: ScrollViewer ( ScrollViewer ) and Cursor (Grid); visual state groups for scrolling up/down, cursor and focus. It is a supported host for the Legend attached properties. docs.text: class Microsoft.Xbox.Controls.NuiTimeline The media timeline used by MediaTransport : a progress bar with markers, position text, a preview thumbnail and a Kinect "gearshift" handle for scrubbing. While loaded, the timeline creates a native scrub tracker (npctrl.dll ordinals 500–510) that follows the engaged Kinect user's hand on the gearshift handle. Dragging the handle zooms the timeline in, moves NuiTimeline.Position , snaps to snappable markers once the user commits, and raises NuiTimeline.ScrubbingStarted , NuiTimeline.Scrubbing and NuiTimeline.ScrubbingCompleted . Scrubbing only happens while NuiTimeline.IsScrubbingEnabled is true , so it needs a Kinect sensor and an engaged user. Template parts: TimelineBarPanel (Panel), TimelinePositionPanel (Panel) and Gearshift ( NuiGearshift ). Visual state groups: ZoomStates (ZoomedIn/ZoomedOut), ThumbnailVisibilityStates and GearshiftVisibiltyStates . The many read-only Interpolated… , …Offset… and …Width properties are layout values computed for the template; apps normally only set the position range, NuiTimeline.Markers and the content properties. docs.text: class Microsoft.Xbox.Controls.Pivot A horizontally swiping tab control: a row of headers above a set of PivotItem pages, with neighbouring pages peeking in from the sides. Items are wrapped in PivotItem containers (or you can add PivotItem objects directly). The user changes pages with the shoulder buttons, D-pad left/right, the remote's previous/next keys, a Kinect swipe or by selecting a header. D-pad up moves focus to the headers; D-pad down or A on a header moves focus back into the selected page. Inside each page, directional focus moves through the page's top-level Grid (see PivotItem.AutoGridNav ). To limit memory use, pages within two positions of the selection are reported as loaded and pages further away as unloaded through Pivot.LoadingPivotItem and Pivot.UnloadingPivotItem ; use these to create and release expensive page content. Each page's PivotItem.VuiCommand is registered with VuiBar.Current while the pivot is loaded; saying it selects and focuses that page. The selected page's command is disabled. Template parts: LayoutRoot , HeadersListElement ( PivotHeadersControl ), PivotItemPresenter (ItemsPresenter) and SwipeElement ( SwipeViewer ). Because the template contains a SwipeViewer , only one swipe-enabled control can be shown per page. docs.text: enum Microsoft.Xbox.Controls.PlayRate Playback rates used by MediaTransport . Negative values rewind, positive values above 1 fast forward; the numeric value is the speed multiplier. Values FastForward128X Fast forward at 128 times normal speed. FastForward16X Fast forward at 16 times normal speed. FastForward2X Fast forward at twice normal speed. This is the first step when the user starts fast forwarding. FastForward32X Fast forward at 32 times normal speed. FastForward4X Fast forward at 4 times normal speed. FastForward64X Fast forward at 64 times normal speed. FastForward8X Fast forward at 8 times normal speed. MaxFastForward The fastest fast-forward rate (same as PlayRate.FastForward128X ). MaxRewind The fastest rewind rate (same as PlayRate.Rewind128X ). NotPlaying Not playing: paused, stopped, closed or buffering. Playing Playing at normal speed. Rewind128X Rewind at 128 times normal speed. Rewind16X Rewind at 16 times normal speed. Rewind2X Rewind at twice normal speed. This is the first step when the user starts rewinding. Rewind32X Rewind at 32 times normal speed. Rewind4X Rewind at 4 times normal speed. Rewind64X Rewind at 64 times normal speed. Rewind8X Rewind at 8 times normal speed.

docs.text: class Microsoft.Xbox.Controls.Rune A single-line text entry control built for the TV: a strip of character tiles the user picks from with the controller or a Kinect hand gesture, with the entered text shown above. Controller: D-pad moves across the tiles, A enters a character, X deletes the last character, the shoulder buttons (or the remote's previous/next keys) jump between letter groups, and Y closes the control when Rune.IsCloseable is true . Kinect: the user hovers over the strip to zoom it and then completes an engagement gesture on a tile to enter it (see RuneTile and RuneCursor ). Tiles switch between letter, extended-letter and number/symbol sets. While a Rune has focus it also accepts text from a chatpad and from a companion-device keyboard, and keeps the companion keyboard in sync. It sets its own A, B, X and Y Legend texts. Native calls go to npctrl.dll ordinals 700–702. The tiles are enabled only while Rune.IsOpen is true ; open it to let the user type. The control raises a TextChanged event when Rune.Text changes. While closed the tiles are disabled and the control is not a tab stop; if focus was inside, it moves to the template's FocusSafeHarbor element. Setting false raises Rune.Closed . It scales with the screen height relative to 720 lines. docs.text: class Microsoft.Xbox.Controls.SwipeViewer Detects Kinect left and right swipe gestures and exposes their progress as events, properties and visual states. The gesture is recognized by the console (npctrl.dll ordinals 300–305); the viewer configures two activation zones and receives callbacks on the UI thread. Without a Kinect sensor or an engaged user, no events are raised. Only one SwipeViewer can be active at a time. A viewer becomes active when it is loaded, enabled and (inside an XboxApplicationFrame ) on the current page; activating a second one throws InvalidOperationException . Pivot and ContinuousList each contain one, so don't place two such controls on the same page, and disable a viewer ( IsEnabled = false ) before showing another. Sequence: SwipeViewer.PeekStarted , then SwipeViewer.PeekProgressChanged as the hand moves into a zone, SwipeViewer.PeekCompleted at full peek, SwipeViewer.SwipeReady , and finally SwipeViewer.SwipeCompleted or SwipeViewer.SwipeFailed . Visual states: LeftNormal / LeftPeeking / LeftSwiped and the matching Right… states; the storyboard of the …Swiped state is played to completion before the side returns to normal. docs.text: class Microsoft.Xbox.Controls.VuiBar The voice user interface (VUI) bar: Kinect speech recognition for the app and the on-screen bar that lists the commands the user can say. Only one instance can exist; it is available as VuiBar.Current . The default XboxApplicationFrame template already contains it, so apps normally do not create one. Creating a second instance throws InvalidOperationException . Typical setup: create one or more VuiGrammar objects with phrases whose semantic values match your commands' VuiCommand.SemanticValue , call VuiBar.LoadGrammar for each, add VuiCommand objects to VuiBar.PrimaryCommands or VuiBar.SecondaryCommands , and call VuiBar.StartRecognition . Grammars can only be loaded or unloaded while recognition is stopped. The phrases for the built-in VuiCommands are loaded automatically. The user says "Xbox" to open the bar (active listening, which times out after 12 seconds without a command). While the bar is open the user can say a command phrase on its own; while it is closed, a command can be said together with the "Xbox" keyword. The two cases use separate confidence thresholds. If a phrase matches several executable commands the bar enters disambiguation and labels the candidates (see VuiBar.SetDisambiguationSlots ). Commands with a VuiCommand.Confirmation ask for confirmation before running. Two fixed commands, Cancel and go Home (with an explicit confirmation), are always available while the bar is open. Speech requires a Kinect sensor, a supported Localization.Culture and speech recognition being enabled in the console settings; check VuiBar.IsCurrentCultureSupported and VuiBar.IsDashSpeechRecognitionEnabled . Changing Localization.Culture stops recognition and unloads all grammars, including the app's. Events and command execution happen on the UI thread. Native calls go to npctrl.dll ordinals 200–218 and 1200. Constructors VuiBar() Properties Microsoft.Xbox.Controls.VuiBarVisibilityState VisibilityState { get; } Gets how the bar is currently displayed. Changes raise VisibilityStateChanged . MediaTransport uses this to make room for the bar. System.Boolean IsActiveListening { get; } Gets whether the bar is open and actively listening for commands. Changes raise VuiBar.ActiveListeningChanged . System.Boolean IsCurrentCultureSupported { get; } Gets whether speech recognition supports the current Localization.Culture . System.Boolean IsDashSpeechRecognitionEnabled { get; } Gets whether the user has speech recognition enabled in the console settings. System.Boolean IsEnabled { get; set; } Gets or sets whether speech recognition is enabled. Setting true while the culture is unsupported throws InvalidOperationException ; the value is ignored when speech is disabled in the console settings. Disabling the bar pauses the recognizer and dismisses any open bar, confirmation or disambiguation. System.Boolean IsRecognitionStarted { get; } Gets whether VuiBar.StartRecognition has been called (and VuiBar.StopRecognition has not). System.Collections.Generic.IList<Microsoft.Xbox.Controls.VuiCommand> ConfirmationCommands { get; } Gets the commands currently offered to confirm or cancel a command. System.Collections.Generic.IList<Microsoft.Xbox.Controls.VuiCommand> ExecutablePrimaryCommands { get; } Gets the subset of VuiBar.PrimaryCommands that can currently execute, in the same order. System.Collections.Generic.IList<Microsoft.Xbox.Controls.VuiCommand> ExecutableSecondaryCommands { get; } Gets the subset of VuiBar.SecondaryCommands that can currently execute, in the same order. System.Collections.Generic.IList<Microsoft.Xbox.Controls.VuiCommand> FixedCommands { get; } Gets the built-in commands that are always available while the bar is open (Cancel and go Home). System.Collections.Generic.IList<Microsoft.Xbox.Controls.VuiCommand> PrimaryCommands { get; } Gets the commands shown prominently on the bar. Adding a command throws InvalidOperationException if it is null , has no VuiCommand.DisplayText or VuiCommand.SemanticValue , needs confirmation but has no VuiCommand.ConfirmationText , is a fixed command, is already on the bar, or shares a semantic value with a command already on the bar. If no loaded grammar contains its semantic value, VuiBar.VuiCommandNotRecognized is raised with VuiCommandNotRecognizedReason.PhraseNotLoaded . System.Collections.Generic.IList<Microsoft.Xbox.Controls.VuiCommand> SecondaryCommands { get; } Gets the less prominent commands shown on the bar. static Microsoft.Xbox.Controls.VuiBar Current { get; } Gets the app's single VuiBar instance. Methods System.Void LoadGrammar(Microsoft.Xbox.Controls.VuiGrammar grammar) Loads a grammar into the speech recognizer so its phrases can be recognized. Throws InvalidOperationException if recognition is started, the grammar is already loaded or it has no phrases. After loading, VuiGrammar.IsLoaded is true and no more phrases can be added. Phrases become active only while a command with the same semantic value is on the bar and can execute. All grammars are unloaded automatically when Localization.Culture changes. System.Void OnApplyTemplate() System.Void SetDisambiguationSlots(System.Collections.Generic.IEnumerable<Microsoft.Xbox.Controls.VuiDisambiguationSlot> slots) Sets the labels used to tell apart commands that match the same phrase. When disambiguation starts, executable commands that have a UI element and VuiCommand.IsDisambiguationEnabled set are assigned slots in order, and each slot's VuiDisambiguationSlot.DisambiguationText is shown as the command's VuiCommand.DisambiguationText . The slot semantic values must match phrases in a loaded grammar. Throws ArgumentException if a slot has empty text or semantic value, or if fewer than VuiBar.MinDisambiguationSlotCount slots are given. System.Void StartRecognition() Starts listening for speech. The recognizer is started on the next dispatcher cycle, and only if the bar is enabled; if the bar is disabled it starts when the bar is enabled. Calling this while already started does nothing. Load your grammars first, because grammars cannot be loaded while recognition is started. System.Void StopRecognition() Stops listening for speech. Call this before loading or unloading grammars. Does nothing if recognition is not started. System.Void UnloadGrammar(Microsoft.Xbox.Controls.VuiGrammar grammar) Removes a loaded grammar from the speech recognizer. Throws ArgumentNullException if grammar is null , and InvalidOperationException if recognition is started. Its phrases cannot be added to again after unloading; create a new grammar instead. Events event System.EventHandler<Microsoft.Xbox.Controls.VuiActiveListeningChangedEventArgs> ActiveListeningChanged Occurs when VuiBar.IsActiveListening changes. Pivot uses this to highlight page headers that can be spoken. event System.EventHandler<Microsoft.Xbox.Controls.VuiBarVisibilityStateChangedEventArgs> VisibilityStateChanged event System.EventHandler<Microsoft.Xbox.Controls.VuiCommandNotRecognizedEventArgs> VuiCommandNotRecognized Occurs when speech was heard but did not run a command, or when a command is added whose phrase is not loaded. Use it for diagnostics or to give the user feedback. See VuiCommandNotRecognizedReason for the possible causes. Fields static System.Int32 MinDisambiguationSlotCount The minimum number of slots that must be passed to VuiBar.SetDisambiguationSlots (1). static System.Windows.DependencyProperty ConfirmationTextProperty Identifies the read-only ConfirmationText dependency property: the VuiCommand.ConfirmationText of the command being confirmed, or empty. The property itself is not public; bind to it from a custom VuiBar template. static System.Windows.DependencyProperty DisambiguationTextProperty Identifies the read-only DisambiguationText dependency property: the localized prompt shown while the user must choose between matching commands. The property itself is not public; bind to it from a custom VuiBar template. static System.Windows.DependencyProperty IsActiveListeningProperty static System.Windows.DependencyProperty IsRecognitionStartedProperty static System.Windows.DependencyProperty ListeningTextProperty Identifies the read-only ListeningText dependency property: the localized prompt the bar shows while listening with no commands to list. The property itself is not public; bind to it from a custom VuiBar template. static System.Windows.DependencyProperty VisibilityStateProperty static System.Windows.DependencyProperty VuiLanguageProperty Identifies the read-only VuiLanguage dependency property: the speech language selected from the current culture (US English by default). docs.text: class Microsoft.Xbox.Controls.VuiCommand A command the user can trigger by voice through the VuiBar . A command is matched to speech through its VuiCommand.SemanticValue : load a VuiGrammar containing one or more phrases with that semantic value, then add the command to VuiBar.PrimaryCommands or VuiBar.SecondaryCommands (or assign it to PivotItem.VuiCommand ). When recognized, the command runs VuiCommand.TargetCommand and raises VuiCommand.Executed . The command is an ICommand , so it can also be bound to buttons. A command can be attached to only one loaded UI element at a time; doing otherwise throws InvalidOperationException . The predefined commands in VuiCommands are built in: their display text, semantic value and confirmation settings cannot be changed. Only commands attached to a Button take part in disambiguation. System.Boolean IsEnabled { get; set; } Gets or sets whether the command may execute. Disabled commands are removed from the executable lists and their phrases are deactivated. MediaTransport and Pivot manage this property for the commands they own. Show the words the user should say. System.String SemanticValue { get; set; } Gets or sets the value that links the command to grammar phrases. Throws InvalidOperationException for built-in commands and while the command is on the bar. The value must be unique among commands on the bar and must not be "xbox" or a built-in semantic value. System.Windows.Input.ICommand TargetCommand { get; set; } Gets or sets an ICommand to run when the voice command executes. The voice command can execute only while the target's CanExecute returns true for VuiCommand.TargetCommandParameter ; its CanExecuteChanged is tracked. System.Void Execute(System.Object parameter) Executes the command: runs VuiCommand.TargetCommand and raises VuiCommand.Executed . Must be called on the UI thread. docs.text: enum Microsoft.Xbox.Controls.VuiCommandNotRecognizedReason Explains why VuiBar.VuiCommandNotRecognized was raised. Values LanguageActiveConfidence The phrase was spoken on its own while the bar was open but its confidence was below the speech language's default threshold. LanguageNormalConfidence The phrase was spoken with the "Xbox" keyword but its confidence was below the speech language's default threshold. None No reason given. PhraseActiveConfidence The phrase was spoken on its own while the bar was open but its confidence was below the phrase's own threshold. PhraseNormalConfidence The phrase was spoken with the "Xbox" keyword but its confidence was below the phrase's own threshold. PhraseNotFound The recognizer returned a rule that does not belong to any loaded phrase. PhraseNotLoaded A command was added to the bar but no loaded grammar contains a phrase with its semantic value, so it can never be spoken. TargetCommandCannotExecute The matching command is enabled but its VuiCommand.TargetCommand cannot execute. VuiCommandDisabled The matching command's VuiCommand.IsEnabled is false . VuiCommandNotFound The phrase was recognized but no command on the bar has its semantic value. WaitingForSelectionAnimation Speech arrived while a previously recognized command was still playing its selection animation. XboxConfidence The "Xbox" keyword spoken with the phrase was recognized with too little confidence.

docs.text: class Microsoft.Xbox.Controls.VuiGrammar A set of spoken phrases, each mapped to a semantic value, that can be loaded into the VuiBar recognizer. Add phrases with VuiGrammar.AddPhrase and then call VuiBar.LoadGrammar while recognition is stopped. Several phrases may share a semantic value (synonyms). docs.text: class Microsoft.Xbox.Controls.XboxApplicationFrame The navigation frame to use as the root of an Xbox Silverlight app. It hosts pages, plays page transitions and contains the app's VuiBar . Creating the frame initializes GamerServices ( GamerServicesDispatcher.Initialize ) and the UI sound system if they are not initialized yet, and pumps the XNA framework and GamerServices dispatchers on every rendered frame. Controls that depend on GamerServices, such as the screen-saver handling in MediaTransport , therefore work automatically inside this frame. The template must contain a VuiBar named PART_VuiBar (the default template does); otherwise InvalidOperationException is thrown. Only one VuiBar may exist per app, so do not add another one when you use this frame. On navigation the old and new pages are shown in two presenters and their navigation transitions (set with the TransitionService attached properties) are played. Elements marked as transition targets animate in order after the page. Any SwipeViewer on the outgoing page is turned off and the one on the incoming page is turned on. Constructors XboxApplicationFrame() Methods System.Void OnApplyTemplate() System.Void OnContentChanged(System.Object oldContent, System.Object newContent) Starts the page transition when the frame's content changes. Completes any transition still in progress, places both pages in the frame's presenters, and starts the out and in transitions once the new page's items controls have loaded (or after 0.3 seconds if it has none).

docs.text: Microsoft.Xbox.Media.Mpeg ¶ Assembly: Microsoft.Xbox.dll Type Summary MpegAudioStreamKey Keys of the dictionary returned by MpegDemultiplexer.GetAudioStreamProperties . MpegContainerType MPEG-2 system container formats. MpegDemultiplexer Splits an MPEG-2 transport stream into its elementary audio, video and caption streams using the console's native demultiplexer. Typically used inside a custom MediaStreamSource to play transport-stream content. MpegElementaryStreamType The coding of an elementary stream. Most values equal the MPEG-2 transport-stream stream_type code. MpegFrameType How a video sample depends on other frames. MpegSampleProperty Flags attached to a demultiplexed sample. MpegStreamSample One demultiplexed elementary-stream sample (an access unit) with its timing information. MpegStreamsNotInitializedException The exception thrown when an MpegDemultiplexer method needs the stream layout before enough input has been processed. Keep calling MpegDemultiplexer.ProcessInput and retry. MpegStreamType Kinds of elementary streams, used to look up stream IDs with MpegDemultiplexer.GetStreamIdAtIndex . MpegVideoStreamKey Keys of the dictionary returned by MpegDemultiplexer.GetVideoStreamProperties . MpegAudioStreamKey ¶ enum Microsoft.Xbox.Media.Mpeg.MpegAudioStreamKey Keys of the dictionary returned by MpegDemultiplexer.GetAudioStreamProperties . Values AudioProfile The codec profile, as a decimal number. Channels The number of audio channels. ChannelsMask The speaker-position mask for the channels, as a decimal number. CodecPrivateData Codec initialization data (up to 128 bytes) as an uppercase hexadecimal string, suitable for the CodecPrivateData media attribute of a MediaStreamSource . Frequency The sampling rate, in Hz. Language The language code declared for the stream. MpegContainerType ¶ enum Microsoft.Xbox.Media.Mpeg.MpegContainerType MPEG-2 system container formats. Values Program MPEG-2 program stream. Not supported; the MpegDemultiplexer constructor throws NotImplementedException . Transport MPEG-2 transport stream (188-byte packets). This is the only supported format. MpegDemultiplexer ¶ class Microsoft.Xbox.Media.Mpeg.MpegDemultiplexer Splits an MPEG-2 transport stream into its elementary audio, video and caption streams using the console's native demultiplexer. Typically used inside a custom MediaStreamSource to play transport-stream content. Feed raw transport-stream bytes with MpegDemultiplexer.ProcessInput . Once MpegDemultiplexer.HasStreamProperties returns true , find streams with MpegDemultiplexer.GetStreamIdAtIndex , enable them with MpegDemultiplexer.SelectStream , read their formats, and pull samples with MpegDemultiplexer.ProduceOutputForStream . Only MpegContainerType.Transport is supported. Dispose the demultiplexer to release the native instance; calls after disposal throw InvalidOperationException . docs.text: class Microsoft.Xbox.Media.Mpeg.MpegDemultiplexer Splits an MPEG-2 transport stream into its elementary audio, video and caption streams using the console's native demultiplexer. Typically used inside a custom MediaStreamSource to play transport-stream content. Feed raw transport-stream bytes with MpegDemultiplexer.ProcessInput . Once MpegDemultiplexer.HasStreamProperties returns true , find streams with MpegDemultiplexer.GetStreamIdAtIndex , enable them with MpegDemultiplexer.SelectStream , read their formats, and pull samples with MpegDemultiplexer.ProduceOutputForStream . Only MpegContainerType.Transport is supported. Dispose the demultiplexer to release the native instance; calls after disposal throw InvalidOperationException . MusicPlayer Controls background music that the user is playing from the console's music player. Sounds Plays the standard console navigation sounds for buttons and lets you replace them per element. Speakers Reports the console's audio output configuration and lets the application force stereo output. TimedTextColor Caption colors that the user can choose in the console's closed-captioning settings. TimedTextEdgeAttribute The edge effect drawn around caption characters. Obtain one from MediaCapabilities.GetTimedTextSettings and apply it when rendering captions; the properties are read-only. MediaCapabilities ¶ class Microsoft.Xbox.Media.MediaCapabilities Reads and changes the console's closed-captioning settings and reports optional media components. At design time the properties return false , setters do nothing, and MediaCapabilities.GetTimedTextSettings returns default settings. Properties static System.Boolean Enable708Captioning { get; set; } Gets or sets whether the media pipeline decodes CEA-708 closed captions embedded in the video stream. static System.Boolean TimedTextEnabled { get; set; } Gets or sets the console-wide closed-captioning on/off state. Check it before showing captions so that you honor the user's system setting. Methods static Microsoft.Xbox.Media.TimedTextSettings GetTimedTextSettings() Gets the user's caption appearance preferences (font, colors, opacity, edge style and language) from the console settings. static System.Boolean IsOptionalMediaUpdateInstalled() Gets whether the console's optional media update is installed. Some codecs and formats are available only after this update. MusicPlayer ¶ class Microsoft.Xbox.Media.MusicPlayer Controls background music that the user is playing from the console's music player. Pause the user's music before playing your own audio or video, and resume it when you are done. Both methods must be called on the UI thread. Methods static System.Void Pause() Pauses the user's background music so that the application's audio can play. Must be called on the UI thread. static System.Void Resume() Resumes background music that was paused with MusicPlayer.Pause . Must be called on the UI thread. Sounds ¶ class Microsoft.Xbox.Media.Sounds Plays the standard console navigation sounds for buttons and lets you replace them per element. Buttons play click, focus and hover sounds automatically. Sounds play only when Sounds.IsEnabled is true , which requires the user to have enabled interface sound effects in the console settings. A custom sound is loaded with Application.GetResourceStream , so the URI must refer to a WAV resource in the application package; each sound is loaded once and cached. Properties static System.Boolean IsDashSoundEffectEnabled { get; } Gets whether interface sound effects are enabled in the console settings. Read once when the runtime initializes the sounds system. static System.Boolean IsEnabled { get; set; } Gets or sets whether the application plays navigation sounds. Defaults to Sounds.DefaultButtonClickUri . static System.Windows.DependencyProperty ButtonFocusUriProperty Identifies the Sounds.ButtonFocusUri attached property: the sound played when a button receives focus. Defaults to Sounds.DefaultButtonFocusUri . static System.Windows.DependencyProperty ButtonHoverUriProperty Identifies the Sounds.ButtonHoverUri attached property: the sound played when the Kinect hand cursor hovers over a button. Defaults to Sounds.DefaultButtonHoverUri . Speakers ¶ class Microsoft.Xbox.Media.Speakers Reports the console's audio output configuration and lets the application force stereo output. All members must be used on the UI thread. Must be read on the UI thread. static System.Boolean Surround { get; } Gets whether the console's audio output is configured for surround sound. Must be read on the UI thread. docs.text: Microsoft.Xbox.Security.XAuth ¶ Assembly: Microsoft.Xbox.Services.dll Type Summary XAuthCompletedEventArgs Provides data for the XAuthTokenRequest.Completed event. XAuthException The exception that is thrown when an Xbox LIVE token (XAuth) operation fails. XAuthService Provides static methods that control the Xbox LIVE token (XAuth) service used by XAuthTokenRequest . XAuthToken Represents an Xbox LIVE security token issued for a signed-in user and a relying party (web service). XAuthTokenRequest Requests an Xbox LIVE security token for a signed-in player and a web service URN, either synchronously or asynchronously. XAuthXuid Represents the Xbox user ID (XUID) of the gamer an Xbox LIVE token was issued for. XAuthCompletedEventArgs ¶ class Microsoft.Xbox.Security.XAuth.XAuthCompletedEventArgs Provides data for the XAuthTokenRequest.Completed event. Check AsyncCompletedEventArgs.Error first; when it is not null it is an XAuthException and XAuthCompletedEventArgs.Token is null. The UserState property contains the request's XAuthTokenRequest.UserData . Properties Microsoft.Xbox.Security.XAuth.XAuthToken Token { get; } Gets the token that was obtained. XAuthException ¶ class Microsoft.Xbox.Security.XAuth.XAuthException The exception that is thrown when an Xbox LIVE token (XAuth) operation fails. The Exception.HResult property holds the failure code returned by the platform, and the message names the operation that failed together with that code in hexadecimal. Constructors XAuthException(System.String function, System.Int32 result) Initializes a new instance of the XAuthException class for a failed operation. XAuthService ¶ class Microsoft.Xbox.Security.XAuth.XAuthService Provides static methods that control the Xbox LIVE token (XAuth) service used by XAuthTokenRequest . Constructors XAuthService() Methods static System.Collections.Generic.Dictionary<System.String,System.String> LoadWhiteList() Returns the list of web service URLs this application may request tokens for. Throws XAuthException if the list cannot be read. static System.Void ReleaseTokens() Clears all cached tokens and cancels pending asynchronous token requests. Each pending request receives a XAuthTokenRequest.Completed callback whose Error is an XAuthException . Call this, for example, when the signed-in user changes. static System.Void Start(System.Boolean overRideBypass) Starts the Xbox LIVE token service for the application. Call once before requesting tokens. Throws XAuthException if the service cannot be started. XAuthToken ¶ class Microsoft.Xbox.Security.XAuth.XAuthToken Represents an Xbox LIVE security token issued for a signed-in user and a relying party (web service). Tokens are obtained through XAuthTokenRequest and cached by XAuthService . Two tokens are considered equal when they belong to the same user and the same relying party; the token bytes are not compared. Constructors XAuthToken() Properties Microsoft.Xbox.Security.XAuth.XAuthXuid UserId { get; } Gets the Xbox user ID of the gamer the token was issued for. System.String AppliesTo { get; } Gets the relying-party identifier the token applies to. Methods System.Boolean Equals(Microsoft.Xbox.Security.XAuth.XAuthToken other) System.Boolean Equals(System.Object other) System.Byte[] GetBytes() Returns a copy of the raw token data. Send the bytes to the relying party in the form that service expects, for example in an HTTP authorization header. System.Int32 CompareTo(Microsoft.Xbox.Security.XAuth.XAuthToken other) Compares this token with another token, ordering by user ID and then by relying-party identifier. System.Int32 GetHashCode() System.String ToString() Operators static System.Boolean op_Equality(Microsoft.Xbox.Security.XAuth.XAuthToken t1, Microsoft.Xbox.Security.XAuth.XAuthToken t2) Determines whether two tokens refer to the same user and relying party. static System.Boolean op_Inequality(Microsoft.Xbox.Security.XAuth.XAuthToken t1, Microsoft.Xbox.Security.XAuth.XAuthToken t2) Determines whether two tokens refer to a different user or relying party. XAuthTokenRequest ¶ class Microsoft.Xbox.Security.XAuth.XAuthTokenRequest Requests an Xbox LIVE security token for a signed-in player and a web service URN, either synchronously or asynchronously. A request object can be used for one token request only; calling a Get method a second time throws ArgumentException . The user must be signed in to Xbox LIVE and the URN must be one the title is allowed to request tokens for (see XAuthService.LoadWhiteList ). Call XAuthService.Start before requesting tokens. Constructors XAuthTokenRequest() Properties System.Object UserData { get; set; } Gets or sets an application-defined object that is returned in the completion event arguments. Methods Microsoft.Xbox.Security.XAuth.XAuthToken GetToken(System.Int32 playerIndex, System.Uri urn) Obtains a token synchronously for the specified player and URN. This call blocks until the service responds, so avoid it on the UI thread. It throws ArgumentException if urn is null, if the request object was already used, or if a XAuthTokenRequest.Completed handler is attached (use GetTokenAsync in that case). Platform failures are reported as XAuthException . System.Void GetTokenAsync(System.Int32 playerIndex, System.Uri urn) Starts an asynchronous request for a token for the specified player and URN. The result is delivered through XAuthTokenRequest.Completed . A token already in the cache is delivered immediately; requests made before the token service is ready are queued until it is. Throws ArgumentException if this request object was already used. Fields System.EventHandler<Microsoft.Xbox.Security.XAuth.XAuthCompletedEventArgs> Completed Occurs when an asynchronous token request finishes, successfully or not. This is a public delegate field rather than an event; assign or combine handlers before calling XAuthTokenRequest.GetTokenAsync . If the token is already cached, the handler runs before GetTokenAsync returns. Otherwise it runs later, possibly on a thread other than the UI thread, so marshal UI updates through the Dispatcher. The sender argument is null. XAuthXuid ¶ class Microsoft.Xbox.Security.XAuth.XAuthXuid Represents the Xbox user ID (XUID) of the gamer an Xbox LIVE token was issued for. Instances are created by the platform and returned from XAuthToken.UserId . Convert to Int64 to read the numeric XUID. Operators static System.Int64 op_Implicit(Microsoft.Xbox.Security.XAuth.XAuthXuid x) Converts an XAuthXuid to its 64-bit numeric XUID.

MovieTrailer A movie trailer. MusicVideo A music video. PodCast A podcast episode. Track A music track. TvEpisode A TV episode. Unknown The kind is not known. Video Other video content. MediaUsageServiceClient ¶ class Microsoft.Xbox.Services.MediaUsageServiceClient Reports playback activity (play, pause, stop and so on) for media items to the Xbox LIVE media usage service. Nothing is sent until MediaUsageServiceClient.UploadUsageEnabled is set to true . Events are queued (up to about 1,000) and posted in batches every 2 seconds by a UI-thread timer, using the Xbox LIVE token of the user at player index 0. Create the client on the UI thread. Constructors MediaUsageServiceClient() Properties System.Boolean UploadUsageEnabled { get; set; } Gets or sets whether usage events are collected and uploaded. The default is false ; while it is false , MediaUsageServiceClient.UploadMediaUsageAsync discards events. static System.String SignalsMediaServiceBaseUrl { get; } Gets the base URL of the media usage service for the environment the console is configured for, derived from NetworkSettings.ActiveServiceEndpoint the first time it is read. The event is timestamped with the current UTC time and sent with the next batch. Does nothing if MediaUsageServiceClient.UploadUsageEnabled is false . Events event System.EventHandler<Microsoft.Xbox.Services.UploadMediaUsageCompletedEventArgs> UploadMediaUsageCompleted Occurs after a batch of usage events has been posted, or when queuing or posting fails. Check AsyncCompletedEventArgs.Error . RatingsServiceClient ¶ class Microsoft.Xbox.Services.RatingsServiceClient Reads and writes media ratings and reviews on the Xbox LIVE ratings service for a signed-in user. Each call first resolves the service URL from the Xbox LIVE service directory (cached until it expires), then sends an HTTP request authorized with the user's Xbox LIVE token. Results arrive through the matching ...Completed event; check AsyncCompletedEventArgs.Error before reading Result . Exceptions during the operation are reported through the event rather than thrown. If the service directory has no entry for the operation, the event is raised with no error and a null Result . Constructors RatingsServiceClient(System.Int32 playerIndex) Creates a ratings client that acts on behalf of the specified user. Methods System.Void DeleteUserRatingAsync(System.String mediaAssetId) Starts deleting the user's rating of a media item. Completion is reported by RatingsServiceClient.DeleteUserRatingCompleted . System.Void DownloadAggregateRatingsAsync(System.String mediaAssetId) Starts downloading the community rating of a media item. The result is reported by RatingsServiceClient.DownloadAggregateRatingsCompleted . System.Void DownloadUserRatingAsync(System.String mediaAssetId) Starts downloading the user's own rating of a media item. The result is reported by RatingsServiceClient.DownloadUserRatingCompleted . System.Void UploadUserRatingAsync(System.String mediaAssetId, System.Double ratingValue, System.String reviewText) Starts saving the user's rating and optional review of a media item. Completion is reported by RatingsServiceClient.UploadUserRatingCompleted . System.Void UploadUserRatingAsync(System.String mediaAssetId, System.Double ratingValue, System.String reviewText, Microsoft.Xbox.Services.UserInterest userInterest) Starts saving the user's rating, optional review and interest for a media item. Completion is reported by RatingsServiceClient.UploadUserRatingCompleted . System.Void UploadUserRatingInterestAsync(System.String mediaAssetId, Microsoft.Xbox.Services.UserInterest userInterest) Starts saving only the user's interest in a media item, without a rating value. Completion is reported by RatingsServiceClient.UploadUserRatingCompleted . Events event System.EventHandler<Microsoft.Xbox.Services.DeleteUserRatingCompletedEventArgs> DeleteUserRatingCompleted Occurs when RatingsServiceClient.DeleteUserRatingAsync finishes. docs.text: class Microsoft.Xbox.Services.MediaUsageServiceClient Reports playback activity (play, pause, stop and so on) for media items to the Xbox LIVE media usage service. Nothing is sent until MediaUsageServiceClient.UploadUsageEnabled is set to true . Events are queued (up to about 1,000) and posted in batches every 2 seconds by a UI-thread timer, using the Xbox LIVE token of the user at player index 0. Create the client on the UI thread. Constructors MediaUsageServiceClient() Properties System.Boolean UploadUsageEnabled { get; set; } Gets or sets whether usage events are collected and uploaded. The default is false ; while it is false , MediaUsageServiceClient.UploadMediaUsageAsync discards events. static System.String SignalsMediaServiceBaseUrl { get; } Gets the base URL of the media usage service for the environment the console is configured for, derived from NetworkSettings.ActiveServiceEndpoint the first time it is read. Methods System.Void UploadMediaUsageAsync(System.String mediaAssetId, Microsoft.Xbox.Services.UsageEventType eventType, Microsoft.Xbox.Services.MediaType mediaType, System.TimeSpan timelineEventTime, System.TimeSpan mediaLength) Queues a playback event for upload. The event is timestamped with the current UTC time and sent with the next batch. Does nothing if MediaUsageServiceClient.UploadUsageEnabled is false . Events event System.EventHandler<Microsoft.Xbox.Services.UploadMediaUsageCompletedEventArgs> UploadMediaUsageCompleted Occurs after a batch of usage events has been posted, or when queuing or posting fails. Check AsyncCompletedEventArgs.Error .

docs.text: class Microsoft.Xbox.Services.RatingsServiceClient Reads and writes media ratings and reviews on the Xbox LIVE ratings service for a signed-in user. Each call first resolves the service URL from the Xbox LIVE service directory (cached until it expires), then sends an HTTP request authorized with the user's Xbox LIVE token. Results arrive through the matching ...Completed event; check AsyncCompletedEventArgs.Error before reading Result . Exceptions during the operation are reported through the event rather than thrown. If the service directory has no entry for the operation, the event is raised with no error and a null Result . Constructors RatingsServiceClient(System.Int32 playerIndex) Creates a ratings client that acts on behalf of the specified user. Methods System.Void DeleteUserRatingAsync(System.String mediaAssetId) Starts deleting the user's rating of a media item. Completion is reported by RatingsServiceClient.DeleteUserRatingCompleted . System.Void DownloadAggregateRatingsAsync(System.String mediaAssetId) Starts downloading the community rating of a media item. The result is reported by RatingsServiceClient.DownloadAggregateRatingsCompleted . System.Void DownloadUserRatingAsync(System.String mediaAssetId) Starts downloading the user's own rating of a media item. The result is reported by RatingsServiceClient.DownloadUserRatingCompleted . Completion is reported by RatingsServiceClient.UploadUserRatingCompleted . Completion is reported by RatingsServiceClient.UploadUserRatingCompleted . Completion is reported by RatingsServiceClient.UploadUserRatingCompleted . On success, Result holds the rating as stored by the service.

Values BackwardIn The element enters during back navigation. BackwardOut The element leaves during back navigation. ForwardIn The element enters during forward navigation. ForwardOut The element leaves during forward navigation. TransitionService ¶ class Microsoft.Xbox.Transitions.TransitionService Attached properties and events that control the animated transitions XboxApplicationFrame plays when navigating between pages. Set NavigationInTransition and NavigationOutTransition on a page to choose its animations; XboxApplicationPage sets both to ZIndexTransition by default. TransitionEventArgs.TargetElement is the new page. event System.EventHandler<Microsoft.Xbox.Transitions.TransitionEventArgs> TransitionOutCompleted Occurs when all of the outgoing page's transitions have finished and the old page has been removed. In this version TransitionEventArgs.TargetElement is always null for this event. event System.EventHandler<Microsoft.Xbox.Transitions.TransitionEventArgs> TransitionOutStarted Occurs when the outgoing page's transitions start. Methods static System.Void dcbf(System.Int32 offset, System.Void* _base) Writes the cache block containing the specified address back to memory if it was modified and removes it from the cache. static System.Void dcbst(System.Int32 offset, System.Void* _base) Writes the cache block containing the specified address back to memory if it was modified, keeping it in the cache. static System.Void dcbt(System.Int32 offset, System.Void* _base) Hints that the cache block containing the specified address will be read soon, so it can be prefetched. static System.Void dcbz(System.Int32 offset, System.Void* _base) Zeroes the data cache block that contains the specified address without reading it from memory first. static System.Void dcbz128(System.Int32 offset, System.Void* _base) Zeroes the 128-byte cache line that contains the specified address without reading it from memory first. Companion ¶ class Microsoft.Xbox.Companion Exchanges messages with SmartGlass companion devices (phones, tablets, PCs) that are connected to the console. The companion session starts when the first handler is attached to any of this class's events and stops, discarding pending send contexts, when the last handler is removed. Keep at least one handler attached for as long as you want to receive companion traffic. All events are posted to the UI thread through the main Dispatcher . FPU ¶ class Microsoft.Xbox.FPU Exposes Xbox 360 (PowerPC) floating-point instructions as methods that the JIT compiler emits inline. These methods let performance-sensitive code use hardware operations such as branch-free selection and fast reciprocal estimates. Estimate instructions trade precision for speed. The conversion methods follow the processor's register conventions: integer results are returned in the bit pattern of a double. Methods static System.Double fabs(System.Double b) Returns the absolute value of a double-precision value. static System.Double fcfid(System.Double b) Converts a 64-bit integer, stored in the bit pattern of a double, to a floating-point value. static System.Double fctid(System.Double b) Converts a value to a 64-bit integer using the current floating-point rounding mode. static System.Double fctidz(System.Double b) Converts a value to a 64-bit integer, rounding toward zero. static System.Double fctiw(System.Double b) Converts a value to a 32-bit integer using the current floating-point rounding mode. static System.Double fctiwz(System.Double b) Converts a value to a 32-bit integer, rounding toward zero. static System.Double fpmax(System.Double a, System.Double b) Returns the larger of two values using branch-free selection. static System.Double fpmin(System.Double a, System.Double b) Returns the smaller of two values using branch-free selection. static System.Double frnd(System.Double b) Applies the processor's floating-point rounding instruction to a value. Verify on the console whether the rounding you need (to an integer or to single precision) matches before relying on this method. static System.Double frsqrte(System.Double b) Computes a fast estimate of the reciprocal square root (1/sqrt(b)). static System.Double fsel(System.Double comparand, System.Double ge, System.Double lt) Selects one of two values according to the sign of a comparand, without branching. static System.Double fsqrt(System.Double b) Computes the square root of a double-precision value. static System.Single fpmax(System.Single a, System.Single b) Returns the larger of two single-precision values using branch-free selection. static System.Single fpmin(System.Single a, System.Single b) Returns the smaller of two single-precision values using branch-free selection. static System.Single fres(System.Double b) Computes a fast single-precision estimate of the reciprocal (1/b). static System.Single fself(System.Single comparand, System.Single ge, System.Single lt) Selects one of two single-precision values according to the sign of a comparand, without branching. static System.Single fsqrts(System.Single b) Computes the square root of a single-precision value. MethodExtensions ¶ class Microsoft.Xbox.MethodExtensions Provides extension methods for Thread that query and set which Xbox 360 hardware thread a managed thread runs on. Both methods operate only on the calling thread; passing any other thread throws InvalidOperationException . Methods static System.Int32 GetCurrentProcessorNumber(System.Threading.Thread thread) Returns the number of the hardware thread the calling thread is currently running on. static System.Void SetProcessorAffinity(System.Threading.Thread thread, System.Int32[] cpus) Moves the calling thread to the specified hardware thread. Throws ArgumentException if cpus is null, and InvalidOperationException if it does not contain exactly one value in the range 0 to 5, if thread is not the current thread, or if the affinity cannot be set. RuntimeHelpers ¶ class Microsoft.Xbox.RuntimeHelpers Provides Xbox 360 runtime services: console language and locale, processor affinity, ahead-of-time compilation of call graphs, and resource helpers. docs.text: class Microsoft.Xbox.FPU Exposes Xbox 360 (PowerPC) floating-point instructions as methods that the JIT compiler emits inline. These methods let performance-sensitive code use hardware operations such as branch-free selection and fast reciprocal estimates. Estimate instructions trade precision for speed. The conversion methods follow the processor's register conventions: integer results are returned in the bit pattern of a double. Methods static System.Double fabs(System.Double b) Returns the absolute value of a double-precision value. static System.Double fcfid(System.Double b) Converts a 64-bit integer, stored in the bit pattern of a double, to a floating-point value. static System.Double fctid(System.Double b) Converts a value to a 64-bit integer using the current floating-point rounding mode. static System.Double fctidz(System.Double b) Converts a value to a 64-bit integer, rounding toward zero. static System.Double fctiw(System.Double b) Converts a value to a 32-bit integer using the current floating-point rounding mode. static System.Double fctiwz(System.Double b) Converts a value to a 32-bit integer, rounding toward zero. static System.Double fpmax(System.Double a, System.Double b) Returns the larger of two values using branch-free selection. static System.Double fpmin(System.Double a, System.Double b) Returns the smaller of two values using branch-free selection. static System.Double frnd(System.Double b) Applies the processor's floating-point rounding instruction to a value. Verify on the console whether the rounding you need (to an integer or to single precision) matches before relying on this method. static System.Double frsqrte(System.Double b) Computes a fast estimate of the reciprocal square root (1/sqrt(b)). static System.Double fsel(System.Double comparand, System.Double ge, System.Double lt) Selects one of two values according to the sign of a comparand, without branching. static System.Double fsqrt(System.Double b) Computes the square root of a double-precision value. static System.Single fpmax(System.Single a, System.Single b) Returns the larger of two single-precision values using branch-free selection. static System.Single fpmin(System.Single a, System.Single b) Returns the smaller of two single-precision values using branch-free selection. static System.Single fres(System.Double b) Computes a fast single-precision estimate of the reciprocal (1/b). static System.Single fself(System.Single comparand, System.Single ge, System.Single lt) Selects one of two single-precision values according to the sign of a comparand, without branching. static System.Single fsqrts(System.Single b) Computes the square root of a single-precision value.
docs.title: FPU

docs.text: class Microsoft.Xbox.MethodExtensions Provides extension methods for Thread that query and set which Xbox 360 hardware thread a managed thread runs on. Both methods operate only on the calling thread; passing any other thread throws InvalidOperationException . Methods static System.Int32 GetCurrentProcessorNumber(System.Threading.Thread thread) Returns the number of the hardware thread the calling thread is currently running on. static System.Void SetProcessorAffinity(System.Threading.Thread thread, System.Int32[] cpus) Moves the calling thread to the specified hardware thread. Throws ArgumentException if cpus is null, and InvalidOperationException if it does not contain exactly one value in the range 0 to 5, if thread is not the current thread, or if the affinity cannot be set.
docs.title: MethodExtensions

docs.text: class Microsoft.Xbox.RuntimeHelpers Provides Xbox 360 runtime services: console language and locale, processor affinity, ahead-of-time compilation of call graphs, and resource helpers. Several members are security critical or reserved for the platform and cannot be called from application code. Applications can use RuntimeHelpers.GetLanguage and RuntimeHelpers.GetLocale , and the extension methods in Microsoft.Xbox.MethodExtensions (System.Core) for processor affinity. Methods static System.Globalization.CultureInfo CreateCustomCultureInfoForResources(System.String name) Creates a culture with the specified name for use in resource lookup. Reserved for platform code. The culture only affects which resources are found; formatting follows the invariant culture. static System.Int32 GetCurrentProcessorNumber(System.Threading.Thread thread) Returns the number of the hardware thread the specified thread is running on. Reserved for platform code. Applications call the GetCurrentProcessorNumber extension method in Microsoft.Xbox.MethodExtensions instead. static System.Int32 SetProcessorAffinity(System.Threading.Thread thread, System.Int32 cpu) Sets the hardware thread the specified thread runs on. Reserved for platform code. Applications call the SetProcessorAffinity extension method in Microsoft.Xbox.MethodExtensions instead. static System.Resources.ResourceManager CreateFileBasedResourceManager(System.String baseName, System.String resourceDir, System.Type usingResourceSet) Creates a resource manager that reads .resources files from a directory instead of from assembly manifests. Reserved for platform code. static System.UInt32 GetLanguage() Returns the language selected in the console's system settings. static System.UInt32 GetLocale() Returns the country or region selected in the console's system settings. static System.Void CompileCallGraph(System.RuntimeMethodHandle method) Compiles the specified method and the methods it calls before they are first executed. Security critical; reserved for platform code. static System.Void CompileCallGraph(System.RuntimeMethodHandle method, System.RuntimeTypeHandle[] instantiation) Compiles the specified generic method instantiation and the methods it calls before they are first executed. Security critical; reserved for platform code. AgeGroup ¶ enum Microsoft.Xna.Framework.GamerServices.AgeGroup Specifies the age group of a gamer profile. Values Adult The profile belongs to an adult. Child The profile belongs to a child. Values Play The content will be played in full. Preview Only a preview (for example a trailer or clip) of the content will be shown. ContentRating ¶ class Microsoft.Xna.Framework.GamerServices.ContentRating Represents a content rating (content type, rating system and level) and checks it against the parental-control settings of signed-in gamers. Build a rating from the constants in the nested Type , System and Level classes, then call CanAccess or CanAccessAsync before playing rated video. Use ContentRating.Unrated for content without a rating. Constructors ContentRating(System.Int32 ratingType, System.Int32 ratingSystem, System.Int32 ratingLevel) Initializes a new rating from a content type, rating system and rating level. Properties System.Int32 RatingLevel { get; } Gets the rating level within the rating system. System.Int32 RatingSystem { get; } Gets the rating system (country or board) of the rating. System.Int32 RatingType { get; } Gets the content type of the rating. System.Object Tag { get; set; } Gets or sets an application-defined object associated with the rating. Methods static System.Boolean CanAccess(System.Collections.Generic.IEnumerable<Microsoft.Xna.Framework.GamerServices.SignedInGamer> gamers, Microsoft.Xna.Framework.GamerServices.ContentRating contentRating) Checks immediately whether the specified gamers may access content with a given rating under their parental-control settings. static System.Void CanAccessAsync(System.Collections.Generic.IEnumerable<Microsoft.Xna.Framework.GamerServices.SignedInGamer> gamers, Microsoft.Xna.Framework.GamerServices.ContentAccessType accessType, Microsoft.Xna.Framework.GamerServices.ContentRating contentRating, System.Object state) Starts an asynchronous parental-control check of whether the specified gamers may access content with a given rating. The result is reported through ContentRating.AccessConfirmationCompleted . Unlike CanAccess, this goes through the system's confirmation path, which can involve system UI. Throws ArgumentNullException if gamers is null. Events event System.EventHandler<Microsoft.Xna.Framework.GamerServices.ContentAccessConfirmationCompletedEventArgs> AccessConfirmationCompleted Occurs when a ContentRating.CanAccessAsync check completes. This is a static event; the sender is null. Raised on a background thread. Fields static Microsoft.Xna.Framework.GamerServices.ContentRating Unrated A shared rating that represents unrated content. Its type is Type.Unrated , its system is 0 and its level is 255. Do not modify its Tag, because the instance is shared. docs.text: class Microsoft.Xna.Framework.GamerServices.ContentRating Represents a content rating (content type, rating system and level) and checks it against the parental-control settings of signed-in gamers. Methods static System.Boolean CanAccess(System.Collections.Generic.IEnumerable<Microsoft.Xna.Framework.GamerServices.SignedInGamer> gamers, Microsoft.Xna.Framework.GamerServices.ContentRating contentRating) Checks immediately whether the specified gamers may access content with a given rating under their parental-control settings. static System.Void CanAccessAsync(System.Collections.Generic.IEnumerable<Microsoft.Xna.Framework.GamerServices.SignedInGamer> gamers, Microsoft.Xna.Framework.GamerServices.ContentAccessType accessType, Microsoft.Xna.Framework.GamerServices.ContentRating contentRating, System.Object state) Starts an asynchronous parental-control check of whether the specified gamers may access content with a given rating. CacheContainer ¶ class Microsoft.Xna.Framework.Storage.CacheContainer A temporary storage area on the console's utility (cache) partition, for downloaded data that can be recreated if lost, such as images or media segments. Use the inherited StorageContainer file methods to read and write files. Only one cache container can be open at a time. Disposing it unmounts the partition. The container is not tied to a user profile; opening it with format set to true erases its content, so treat it as a cache rather than a place for user data. Methods static Microsoft.Xna.Framework.Storage.CacheContainer EndOpenCacheContainer(System.IAsyncResult result) Completes mounting the cache partition and returns the container. Blocks until the mount has finished. static System.IAsyncResult BeginOpenCacheContainer(System.AsyncCallback callback, System.Object state) Starts mounting the cache partition with default settings (no format, 4,096-byte clusters, minimum file cache). static System.IAsyncResult BeginOpenCacheContainer(System.Boolean format, System.Int32 bytesPerCluster, System.Int32 fileCacheSize, System.AsyncCallback callback, System.Object state) Starts mounting the cache partition with the specified settings. The mount runs on a thread-pool thread.

docs.text: System.Reflection ¶ Assembly: mscorlib.dll Type Summary ReflectionPermissionFrame Represents a runtime stack frame that temporarily relaxes reflection permission checks for the code that pushes it. ReflectionPermissionFrame ¶ struct System.Reflection.ReflectionPermissionFrame Represents a runtime stack frame that temporarily relaxes reflection permission checks for the code that pushes it. This structure is security critical and used by the platform itself; application code cannot use it. Methods System.Void Pop() Removes the frame from the current thread's frame chain. System.Void Push(System.Reflection.ReflectionPermissionFrame.PermissionFlag flag) Pushes the frame onto the current thread's frame chain with the specified permissions. Every Push must be matched by a call to ReflectionPermissionFrame.Pop on the same thread.
