MagneticZone ¶ enum System.Windows.Input.MagneticZone Identifies the concentric zones around a magnetic button's origin that govern how the Kinect hand cursor snaps to it, from innermost to outermost. The zone sizes are set with Button.MagneticRadii and the time spent in each zone before the cursor attaches or detaches with Button.MagneticDelays . Values Approach The zone in which the cursor is approaching the button but does not attach. FastAttach The innermost zone; the cursor attaches after the short fast-attach delay. FastDetach The outermost zone; an attached cursor detaches after the short fast-detach delay. SlowAttach The zone outside MagneticZone.FastAttach ; the cursor attaches after the longer slow-attach delay. SlowDetach The zone in which an attached cursor detaches after the slow-detach delay. SpeechCommand ¶ class System.Windows.Input.SpeechCommand Base class for an ICommand that can also be invoked by voice, and that ties a phrase to a Button . Derive from this class, implement SpeechCommand.DisplayText , SpeechCommand.CanExecute and SpeechCommand.Execute , and assign an instance to a button's Command property. While the button is loaded, the command is linked to it. When the command reports a voice activation by calling SpeechCommand.OnInternalExecuted , the button raises Click with InputModality.Voice , which then executes the command. The button's IsEnabled state is combined with SpeechCommand.CanExecute to decide whether the phrase is available. A command instance can be linked to only one loaded button at a time. Voice input requires a Kinect sensor. The button template can define the SpeechHidden, SpeechShown and SpeechDisambiguating visual states to show the phrase on screen. Constructors SpeechCommand() Properties System.String DisambiguationText { get; } Gets the extra text shown when several commands share the same phrase and the user must choose between them. System.String DisplayText { get; set; } When overridden in a derived class, gets or sets the phrase the user says to invoke the command, as it is shown on screen. Methods System.Boolean CanExecute(System.Object parameter) When overridden in a derived class, determines whether the command can run. System.Void Execute(System.Object parameter) When overridden in a derived class, performs the command's action. System.Void OnCanExecuteChanged() Raises the SpeechCommand.CanExecuteChanged event unconditionally. System.Void OnInternalExecuted() Reports that the command was invoked by voice. The linked Button responds by raising Click with InputModality.Voice , which in turn calls SpeechCommand.Execute . Nothing happens if no loaded button is linked to the command, or if the button is already executing its command. System.Void OnPropertyChanged(System.String propertyName) Raises the SpeechCommand.PropertyChanged event. System.Void UpdateCanExecute() Re-evaluates SpeechCommand.CanExecute with a null parameter and raises SpeechCommand.CanExecuteChanged if the result differs from the previous one. Call this whenever the state that SpeechCommand.CanExecute depends on changes, so the voice phrase is enabled or disabled to match. Events event System.ComponentModel.PropertyChangedEventHandler PropertyChanged Occurs when a property value changes, for example SpeechCommand.DisplayText . event System.EventHandler CanExecuteChanged Occurs when the result of SpeechCommand.CanExecute changes. Raised by SpeechCommand.OnCanExecuteChanged , and by SpeechCommand.UpdateCanExecute when it detects a change. UserInformation ¶ class System.Windows.Input.UserInformation Identifies the user who produced an input event: the controller slot for controller input, and the Kinect tracking ID for gesture input. Instances are created by the platform. When a value is not known, the properties hold UserInformation.InvalidPlayerIndex and UserInformation.InvalidTrackingId . Properties System.Int32 PlayerIndex { get; } Gets the player (controller slot) index of the user who produced the input. System.Int32 TrackingId { get; } Gets the Kinect tracking ID of the body that produced the input. Fields const System.Int32 InvalidPlayerIndex The value of UserInformation.PlayerIndex when no player is associated with the input. This field is constant (254). const System.Int32 InvalidTrackingId The value of UserInformation.TrackingId when no tracked body is associated with the input. This field is constant (0).

docs.text: enum System.Windows.Input.MagneticZone Identifies the concentric zones around a magnetic button's origin that govern how the Kinect hand cursor snaps to it, from innermost to outermost. The zone sizes are set with Button.MagneticRadii and the time spent in each zone before the cursor attaches or detaches with Button.MagneticDelays . Values Approach The zone in which the cursor is approaching the button but does not attach. FastAttach The innermost zone; the cursor attaches after the short fast-attach delay. FastDetach The outermost zone; an attached cursor detaches after the short fast-detach delay. SlowAttach The zone outside MagneticZone.FastAttach ; the cursor attaches after the longer slow-attach delay. SlowDetach The zone in which an attached cursor detaches after the slow-detach delay.

docs.text: class System.Windows.Input.SpeechCommand Base class for an ICommand that can also be invoked by voice, and that ties a phrase to a Button . Derive from this class, implement SpeechCommand.DisplayText , SpeechCommand.CanExecute and SpeechCommand.Execute , and assign an instance to a button's Command property. While the button is loaded, the command is linked to it. When the command reports a voice activation by calling SpeechCommand.OnInternalExecuted , the button raises Click with InputModality.Voice , which then executes the command. The button's IsEnabled state is combined with SpeechCommand.CanExecute to decide whether the phrase is available. A command instance can be linked to only one loaded button at a time. Voice input requires a Kinect sensor. The button template can define the SpeechHidden, SpeechShown and SpeechDisambiguating visual states to show the phrase on screen. Constructors SpeechCommand() Properties System.String DisambiguationText { get; } Gets the extra text shown when several commands share the same phrase and the user must choose between them. System.String DisplayText { get; set; } When overridden in a derived class, gets or sets the phrase the user says to invoke the command, as it is shown on screen. Methods System.Boolean CanExecute(System.Object parameter) When overridden in a derived class, determines whether the command can run. System.Void Execute(System.Object parameter) When overridden in a derived class, performs the command's action. System.Void OnCanExecuteChanged() Raises the SpeechCommand.CanExecuteChanged event unconditionally. System.Void OnInternalExecuted() Reports that the command was invoked by voice. The linked Button responds by raising Click with InputModality.Voice , which in turn calls SpeechCommand.Execute . Nothing happens if no loaded button is linked to the command, or if the button is already executing its command. System.Void OnPropertyChanged(System.String propertyName) Raises the SpeechCommand.PropertyChanged event. System.Void UpdateCanExecute() Re-evaluates SpeechCommand.CanExecute with a null parameter and raises SpeechCommand.CanExecuteChanged if the result differs from the previous one. Call this whenever the state that SpeechCommand.CanExecute depends on changes, so the voice phrase is enabled or disabled to match. Events event System.ComponentModel.PropertyChangedEventHandler PropertyChanged Occurs when a property value changes, for example SpeechCommand.DisplayText . event System.EventHandler CanExecuteChanged Occurs when the result of SpeechCommand.CanExecute changes. Raised by SpeechCommand.OnCanExecuteChanged , and by SpeechCommand.UpdateCanExecute when it detects a change.
docs.title: SpeechCommand

PRNDReceiver ¶ class System.Windows.Media.PRNDReceiver A PlayReady-ND (network device) receiver: obtains licenses for protected content from a PlayReady-ND transmitter on the local network. Call PRNDReceiver.OpenAsync , then PRNDReceiver.PerformHandshakeAsync , then PRNDReceiver.AcquireLicenseAsync for each item; wait for each step's completion event before the next. Pass PRNDReceiver.SessionId to the media pipeline with MediaSourceAttributesKeys.PRNDSessionID . Exceptions thrown by your event handlers are swallowed. Constructors PRNDReceiver() Properties System.Byte[] SessionId { get; } Gets the identifier of the receiver's current session. System.Int32 HandshakeAlertInterval { get; set; } Gets or sets how long after a successful handshake PRNDReceiver.PRNDReceiverHandshakeAlert is raised, in minutes. Set it before the handshake; the timer is started when the handshake completes. Methods System.Void AcquireLicenseAsync(System.Windows.Media.ContentIdentifierType contentIdentifierType, System.Byte[] contentIdentifier, System.Byte[] customDataTypeId, System.Byte[] customData) Starts acquiring a license for one content item from the transmitter. Completion is reported by PRNDReceiver.PRNDReceiverAcquireLicenseCompleted . System.Void Close() Closes the receiver and cancels any pending handshake alert. The receiver can then be opened again. System.Void OpenAsync(System.Uri transmitterUri) Starts connecting to a PlayReady-ND transmitter. Completion is reported by PRNDReceiver.PRNDReceiverOpenCompleted . System.Void PerformHandshakeAsync(System.Byte[] customDataTypeId, System.Byte[] customData) Starts the registration handshake with the transmitter, optionally sending custom data. Completion is reported by PRNDReceiver.PRNDReceiverPerformHandshakeCompleted . The handshake may be repeated on an open receiver. Events event System.EventHandler PRNDReceiverHandshakeAlert Occurs once, PRNDReceiver.HandshakeAlertInterval minutes after a successful handshake, to signal that the handshake (proximity check) should be repeated. Raised on the UI thread by a dispatcher timer. The event arguments are null. PRNDReceiver.Close cancels the pending alert. event System.EventHandler<System.Windows.Media.PRNDReceiverAcquireLicenseCompletedEventArgs> PRNDReceiverAcquireLicenseCompleted Occurs when PRNDReceiver.AcquireLicenseAsync finishes. event System.EventHandler<System.Windows.Media.PRNDReceiverOpenCompletedEventArgs> PRNDReceiverOpenCompleted Occurs when PRNDReceiver.OpenAsync finishes. If AsyncCompletedEventArgs.Error is null the receiver is open and ready for a handshake; otherwise it holds a PRNDException . event System.EventHandler<System.Windows.Media.PRNDReceiverPerformHandshakeCompletedEventArgs> PRNDReceiverPerformHandshakeCompleted Occurs when PRNDReceiver.PerformHandshakeAsync finishes. On success the receiver can acquire licenses, and the timer for PRNDReceiver.PRNDReceiverHandshakeAlert starts. Fields const System.Int32 IdByteCount The length, in bytes, of session IDs and custom data type IDs (16). This field is constant. const System.Int32 MaxHandshakeAlertInterval The largest value accepted by PRNDReceiver.HandshakeAlertInterval : 2880 minutes (48 hours). This field is constant.
